title: Fire eliminated after narrow defeat by Spirit
description: Welsh Fire are eliminated from The Hundred as they suffer a six-run defeat by London Spirit in their final group phase match in Cardiff.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Sophia Gardens

London Spirit 131-8 (100 balls): Bairstow 34 (19); Jansen 2-16

Welsh Fire 125-7 (100 balls): Cox 44 (28); Willey 3-20

Welsh Fire were eliminated from The Hundred as they suffered a six-run defeat by London Spirit in their final group phase match in Cardiff.

Fire finished their campaign four points behind Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds, who are second and third respectively, with four wins from eight matches.

MI London, who are fourth, can still qualify for the Eliminator at the expense of Sunrisers if they defeat Birmingham Phoenix by a significant margin today.

Heading into their final fixture, the Welsh side's hopes of progressing were effectively over because of their net run-rate of -1.001, and they were handed a target of 132 by Spirit to chase down.

Fire looked on course for a routine win as Joe Root and Jordan Cox produced a 47-run stand to take them to 90-2.

Root departed for a run-a-ball 31 but Cox accelerated to reach 44 from 28 balls, leaving his side needing 15 runs to win from eight balls with six wickets in hand.

But Fire then lost Tom Kohler-Cadmore and Rachin Ravindra in quick succession, with Marco Jansen needing a six from the final ball to level the score.

Jansen slapped David Willey over midwicket hoping to clear the rope but was caught by Jamie Overton at deep as they finished narrowly short.

Sent out to bat first, Spirit never fully gained momentum as the Fire bowlers produced a disciplined display to restrict the visitors to 131-8 in Cardiff.

Jonny Bairstow's 34 from 19 balls provided the early impetus for Spirit while James Coles and Jamie Overton also added 29 and 21 respectively.

But none were able to convert their starts into a substantial innings as Chris Woakes and Jansen picked up two wickets apiece.

Spirit ended their campaign seventh in the table with three wins.

Today is the last day of the group phase so the competition takes a very brief break on Thursday before the knockouts start on Friday.

Both the men's and women's Eliminator matches will take place at The Oval with Sunrisers Leeds facing Southern Brave in the women's contest from 14:15 BST.

Manchester Super Giants will be in the men's Eliminator from 18:00 with their opponent still to be determined.

The finals at Lord's follow on Sunday with Trent Rockets men's and women's sides awaiting the winners of the Eliminators.

title: Perry fifty takes Phoenix to victory over MI London
description: Ellyse Perry hits a superb 62 not out to lead Birmingham Phoenix to a five-wicket victory over MI London in The Hundred.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Edgbaston

MI London 120-6 (100 balls): Henry 42 (33); Gray 2-29

Birmingham Phoenix 121-5 (94 balls): Perry 62* (39); Gordon 2-20

Birmingham Phoenix won by five wickets

Ellyse Perry hit a superb unbeaten half-century to lead Birmingham Phoenix to a five-wicket victory over MI London in The Hundred.

The Australia great finished on 62 not out from 39 balls as Phoenix, set 121 to win, got over the line with six balls to spare at Edgbaston.

It is just a second win of a difficult campaign for Phoenix but one that ensures they leapfrog MI London and avoid finishing bottom of the women's table.

Having opted to chase, Phoenix were quickly on top as they reduced MI London to 29-3 and then 47-4, before a 57-run stand between West Indies' Chinelle Henry and captain Hollie Armitage helped get the visitors up to 120-6.

It looked like being enough as Phoenix lost Alice Capsey and Emma Lamb in quick succession to slip to 48-4 in reply.

But Perry remained and the 35-year-old showed all of her class and experience to control the chase from there.

Fatima Sana provided the support Perry needed, scoring 36 from 32 in a fifth-wicket partnership of 66.

The Pakistan skipper couldn't quite see it through and it was left to Perry, who hit seven fours and two sixes in a classy knock, to finish the job - drilling a four through mid-off to level the scores before winning it with a delicate scoop.

Welsh Fire 138-7 (100 balls): Wareham 50 (34); Harris 3-15

London Spirit 123 (99 balls): Dean 27 (20); Potts 3-23

Georgia Wareham hit her first half-century in The Hundred as Welsh Fire ended their campaign with a comfortable 15-run win over London Spirit.

With both sides already eliminated, only pride was at stake at Sophia Gardens, and Wareham's 33-ball fifty proved decisive.

The Australia all-rounder took Fire to a winning total of 138-7 with a fine late assault to rescue an innings that had stalled following a fast start.

Spirit were soon in trouble in the chase as Fire seamer Grace Potts removed the top three inside the powerplay, taking two in two balls to dismiss Grace Harris and Marie Kelly.

Skipper Charlie Dean helped get her side back into the game as she shared useful partnerships with Charis Pavely and then Nadine de Klerk but when Dean fell for 27, Spirit were 75-6 and struggling.

Fire were in control but while Deandra Dottin remained, Spirit had hope.

The big-hitting West Indian was left too much to do, though, and when she was dismissed with five balls remaining, any lingering doubt over the outcome evaporated.

Fire end their campaign fifth in the table with Spirit sixth.

title: Anna Huang, 17, rises up in Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings
description: Huang closed with an eagle on her final hole and won by two shots over Charley Hull at the PIF London on Sunday.
fullText:
With so much attention on youth the last few weeks, don't overlook Anna Huang. She made it through Ladies European Tour qualifying at age 16, and the Canadian has not missed a beat.

Huang was caught in a duel with Charley Hull on Sunday in the PIF London and held her nerve. Hull four-putted for double bogey on the 17th hole and Huang closed with an eagle to win by two. The 17-year-old now has four LET victories in the last 11 months.

When she won in Morocco in May, Huang became the youngest player with three LET wins, surpassing records previously held by Lydia Ko.

"I've always looked up to Lydia, she's always been my idol growing up. There's so much to admire about her game. She's so calm and composed," Huang said.

Huang's fourth victory allowed her to break into the top 50 in the women's world ranking at No. 43, and she moved to No. 2 behind Casandra Alexander on the tour's Order of Merit.

title: Hull lets late lead slip as Huang, 17, wins again
description: England's Charley Hull lets slip a one-shot lead with two holes to play at the PIF London Championship as 17-year-old Anna Huang wins her fourth event on the Ladies' European Tour.
fullText:
-22 A Huang (Can); -20 C Hull (Eng); -17 S Tan (Sin); -15 P Tavatanakit (Tha), -14 K Bennett (Aus)

Selected others: -12 A Hewson (Eng); -11 L Hall (Wal); -10 G Hall (Eng), A Donegan (Ire)

England's Charley Hull let slip a one-shot lead with two holes to play at the PIF London Championship as 17-year-old Anna Huang won her fourth Ladies' European Tour (LET) event.

The 30-year-old Hull was on course for her 10th professional title and sixth LET success, but four-putted the penultimate hole for a double bogey, while Huang eagled the last to win by two shots.

"That was probably the most thrilling round of golf of my life, that was crazy, I'm just so shocked," the Canadian told the LET website.

"I knew coming down three tough holes was not easy and I tried to focus on each shot because anything can happen in golf and I stayed in my own lane.

"I can't believe I made another eagle. I focused on the putt and made a good stroke, and it went in.

"Charley is such a phenomenal player and playing with her in the past two days in the final group has been really cool. The crowds have been cheering really loud, so it was really fun to be part of the last group."

The tournament took place at Centurion Club, near St Albans, and Huang led after the first round with a six-under round of 67.

Hull's first round on Thursday had been a one-over 74, but she catapulted herself into contention with an 11-under 62 on Friday to equal the lowest round in LET history and break the course record at the Centurion Club.

Huang's best round came on Saturday with an eight-under 65 and she began the last round with a three-stroke advantage.

Birdies on the sixth, ninth, 13th, 15th and 16th took Hull into the lead by one shot, but that disappointing double-bogey five on the par-three 17th handed the advantage back to Huang and she finished in style.

Hull, who birdied the last for a 69, finished on 20 under to be three clear of Singapore's Shannon Tan, with Thailand's Patty Tavatanakit fourth on 15 under.

title: Unmasking London City's Spanish superstar
description: Alexia Putellas' arrival at London City Lionesses was the biggest transfer in WSL history - but who is the person behind the global stardom?
fullText:
There is not a single empty seat as Alexia Putellas walks into a room at a hotel in Maidstone ready to speak to the English media for the first time.

"Woah," the two-time Ballon d'Or winner says as she opens the door and sees all the journalists looking in her direction, eager to finally meet her.

You would think that somebody who is referred to as 'La Reina' - the queen - in Spain is used to that kind of attention.

She is considered one of the greatest players of her generation, captained Barcelona to a fourth Women's Champions League title in May and is a World Cup winner with Spain.

But Putellas, who signed for London City Lionesses this summer in what is being touted as the biggest signing in WSL history, is embarking on a different journey with her new club that brings all the stresses and uncertainties anyone would face.

She sat down with the BBC's Women's Football Weekly podcast and addressed media in a press conference that helped unmask the global superstar.

From Barcelona to Bromley: Inside Putellas' move to LCL

Putellas was born in a municipality of Catalonia called Mollet del Valles in the province of Barcelona, and regularly watched games at Nou Camp as a child.

Former Spain and Barcelona star Andres Iniesta was an inspiration to her, while she has also named Brazilian duo Rivaldo and Ronaldinho as players she idolised.

Putellas attended summer football camps ran by Xavi and played for local side CE Sabadell as a child.

She spent a year at La Masia, Barcelona's famous youth academy, but had to leave when her girls team was disbanded.

After spells at Espanyol and Levante, she eventually returned to Barca in 2012 - the start of an incredible 14-year career with her childhood club.

"In Spain, football is the typical sport. When I was young, [it was] not for women, but fortunately, nowadays it is," said Putellas.

"I just had the ball at my feet and I was playing all the time - in the park, in the streets, sometimes at home.

"For me, it was normal because in my house Barca games were always on the TV. I started by watching games and then suddenly, I had the ball all day."

The 32-year-old went on to win 38 trophies with Barcelona, including 10 league titles and four European cups.

She was awarded back-to-back Ballon d'Or crowns in 2021 and 2022 and is favourite to win it again this year.

Internationally, she helped Spain win the 2023 World Cup and finish runners-up at Euro 2025.

But Putellas is not done. When asked if she can still get better, she laughed and said: "Yeah, of course. Always. Day after day, I want to learn things.

"That's the way I see this job. Just keep going, never stop and be as good as I can."

She described the journey she has embarked on at London City Lionesses as one that can help her "find where my limits are" as a footballer.

Putellas is enjoying pre-season but her focus never fully switches off.

"It's all about Manchester United," she says as she looks ahead to London City's season opener on 4 September (19:00 BST).

She has given up Champions League football to join London City, an independent women's-only club in its infancy. Will she need to adapt her mindset?

"Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I'm going to bring to the project whatever it needs from me," she added.

"I'm 100% committed. I'm hungry to win, I'm hungry to be better day after day and to fight with my team-mates for the victory."

Her competitiveness shines through in every conversation.

She is handed a present - a game based on the London underground - by BBC Sport.

"Oh yes, I will play with Freya Godfrey, then I can win. I will tell her that," she jokes.

That winning mentality has never changed - but she gained a new perspective when an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury ruled her out of Euro 2022 on the eve of the tournament.

"Since the ACL injury, I enjoy everything. It's not enjoying just having fun, it's about learning something, and then I enjoy learning that thing," she added.

"I'm just a person who loves what she does. I love competition, I love football, I love training, I love to improve.

"I'm just always looking forward to better things and that's why I'm here too, because I always need to be moving as a person and a player."

Putellas is still learning the English language. She reminds journalists of that when she tries to breakdown the WSL's tactics.

"Sorry guys, I'm learning football language. This press conference maybe came early!" she jokes.

Her best friend and team mate Jana Fernandez will likely help her learn quickly, as well as several other Spaniards, including summer signing Mapi Leon from Barcelona.

But she has a better grasp of English than she realises and it is clear by the way she talks that her footballing brain is unique.

Her manager Eder Maestre says Putellas is like a secondary coach on the training pitch and has the ability to conduct the way the team plays.

"In my opinion, if I give you a pass without speaking, you have information. That's one thing I learned in Barcelona," she told the BBC.

"Maybe I am giving you that pass because I want them to receive a message like 'we go' or 'we stay.' If it's a stronger pass, it's for them to control or I want them to switch the game or whatever - it's just football language.

"Maybe I improved that in Barcelona because of the style of play. The best drills I ever trained in is about understanding what's happening in the game.

"If you understand what's happening in the game, you will get one step ahead of the opponents. When I'm training, I try to understand the way we want to play."

Putellas' fame is widespread and her grandeur was epitomised by her London City unveiling alongside billionaire owner Michele Kang in New York.

There was an emotional outpouring at her Barca departure on social media and she has 3.4m followers on Instagram.

A mural of Putellas dressed as a superhero was painted in her hometown and Nike gifted her a custom gold crown following her second Ballon d'Or victory.

"I try to not think about it, and just be like, I don't know if the word is normal, but just be me. For me, it's normal to be me," said Putellas.

She admitted walking into her first English press conference was "a little scary" and she does not generally enjoy being the centre of attention.

Her favourite part of the media day, she joked, was getting away from the cameras.

Even in the dressing room, where she is no doubt idolised by those around her, she says having former team-mates like Leon there "makes her feel more confident".

But despite the shyness, Putellas does not look out of place in the limelight. She has an obvious aura and instantly eases apprehension with humour.

In an exchange about her passing on her crown at Barcelona she quickly interjects: "No, I didn't have a crown! It's just media stuff!"

She adds: "I was just like another team-mate and so I feel like that, even if they call me 'La Reina.'

"I don't think anybody else needs to imagine 'I have a crown' and all of this because they are so good, they don't need anything from me.

"I just hope I left the team in a better position than when I started. That would make me feel so good and I enjoyed playing with them - I hope they enjoyed it as well."

Putellas' first few weeks at London City have been full of the challenges that most normal people experience - searching for a house, learning to drive in London, adapting to a new culture and developing her English.

"I have been looking for an apartment. [It's] not cheap. Well, in Barcelona, it's not cheap as well!" she said.

"Looking for where I have to go for shopping, just normal things that in Barcelona, of course, I knew. Now, here, everything is new. There's a lot of traffic here."

She has had family over to visit and has created a list of things to do in London with best friend and team-mate Fernandez.

Putellas was hoping to have dinner with England international and ex-Barcelona team-mate Keira Walsh last week but it had to be postponed.

Her friends in the WSL did give Putellas a warm welcome though...

"Well, some of them told me that it's a hard league and they're going to kick me! But no problem, I'm ready for that. No, I'm just joking...

"[They said] just enjoy the league because the games are crazy and even if you go to an away game, it's something different, something special."

Most of all, Putellas is learning to adapt to the English way of life.

She has tried a full English breakfast - but is not a fan of baked beans - and her TikTok algorithm is already throwing up typical conversational words like "innit".

"I tried an English breakfast. It's quite different from Spain. [I didn't like] the beans, but the sausages and eggs... It was fine," she joked.

"For Spanish people it's weird. Normally, we [have beans] with dinner or lunch, but not for breakfast. I don't know English culture yet!

"The weather is not bad now but I say that and people tell me, 'okay, wait for October and November.'"

But while Putellas is still adapting to life in England, it is clear she is ready to perform for London City Lionesses in September.

Her debut is likely to attract widespread attention and she hopes to embrace the occasion - after all, this is the challenge she craved.

title: Rockets beat MI London to reach knockout stage
description: Trent Rockets book their place in the knockout stages of the men's Hundred with a six-wicket victory against MI London at The Oval.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, The Oval

MI London 147-7 (100 balls): S Curran 72 (46); Gregory 2-32

Trent Rockets 148-4 (90 balls): Santner 52* (23); Gleeson 2-27

Trent Rockets won by six wickets

Trent Rockets booked their place in the knockout stages of the men's Hundred with a six-wicket victory against MI London at The Oval.

Rockets' sixth win in seven matches guarantees them a top-three finish as they moved to 24 points at the top - eight more than the trio of Sunrisers Leeds, Welsh Fire and MI London.

Rockets made a shaky start chasing 148 as Finn Allen fell to Tom Curran before Aneurin Donald and Sam Billings also departed, leaving them 46-3 after 30 balls.

Ben Duckett made 27 from 26 balls before he was dismissed by Richard Gleeson halfway through the innings, but Tim David and Mitchell Santner took full advantage of dropped catches - by Sam Curran and Sherfane Rutherford respectively - to steer their side to a sixth consecutive win.

David finished unbeaten on 32, while New Zealand white-ball captain Santner raced to his maiden Hundred half-century from 21 deliveries and struck the winning runs with 10 balls to spare - sealing Rockets' first victory at the Oval in the competition.

Earlier, after being sent out to bat first, MI London made a rapid start, with the in-form Will Jacks, who had three fifties in four matches, looking in ominous touch again - but two brilliant pieces of fielding halted their early momentum.

First, David produced a superb catch running backwards to remove James Vince, before Duckett's pinpoint direct hit while on the floor ran out Nicholas Pooran two balls later to leave the home side reeling at 35-2.

Jacks and captain Sam Curran then undertook a rebuilding job before the opener departed for 39, courtesy of a stunning reflex return catch by leg-spinner Calvin Harrison.

Wickets continued to fall at regular intervals for the hosts, but Sam Curran brought up a 30-ball half-century - finishing with 72 off 46 balls including four fours and five sixes.

He was dismissed on the final ball of the innings as MI London posted 147-7.

It is a crucial Hundred double-header on Sunday as Sunrisers Leeds host Welsh Fire at Headingley, while London Spirit welcome Birmingham Phoenix to Lord's, with the women's games at 11:00 BST and 14:30, and the men's at 14:30 and 18:00 respectively.

The women's race is still alive for the Sunrisers and Fire, with both needing to win to keep themselves in contention to make the knockout phase, while Spirit and Phoenix are already eliminated.

In the men's competition, Sunrisers and Fire remain in the hunt for the finals, but both Spirit and Phoenix are out of contention.

title: Sciver-Brunt guides Rockets to Hundred knockouts, Super Giants beat Brave
description: Nat Sciver-Brunt's stylish 67 fires Trent Rockets into The Hundred knockout stage with an emphatic nine-wicket win over MI London, while Manchester Super Giants beat Southern Brave.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, The Oval

MI London 121-5 (100 balls): Chathli 31 (27); Bates 3-13

Trent Rockets 125-1 (82 balls): Sciver-Brunt 67* (36); Norris 1-26

Trent Rockets won by nine wickets

Nat Sciver-Brunt made a stylish unbeaten 67 as Trent Rockets booked their spot in the knockout stage of The Hundred with an emphatic nine-wicket win over MI London.

Sciver-Brunt hit nine fours and one six in her knock off 36 balls, which helped the Rockets chase down 122 for victory at The Oval.

It was the England captain's first 50 in this year's tournament and her 11th in The Hundred overall.

Sciver-Brunt shared a tournament record second-wicket stand of 118 with Australian Beth Mooney, who finished on 54 not out off 44 balls, as the Rockets breezed past the target with 18 balls to spare.

Victory for the Rockets puts them four points above second-placed Southern Brave.

The Rockets face Brave in their final group match on Monday but have a significantly better net run-rate (+1.601) compared with their opponents (+0.148) so have one foot in the final.

Earlier, Samantha Bates had taken 3-13 to help restrict MI to a modest 121-5.

Bates had the dangerous Hayley Matthews lbw for 10 early on then the left-arm spinner claimed two wickets in two balls to leave MI struggling at 49-4.

Bates trapped top scorer Kira Chathli lbw for 31 before Nicola Carey was stumped next ball following a smart piece of glovework by Beth Mooney.

The 30-year-old Aussie thought she had a hat-trick when Alice Monaghan was given out lbw, only for the decision to be overturned on review with the ball sliding down leg.

Monaghan and Chinelle Henry led the fightback - both players finishing unbeaten on 27 off 21 balls - as they helped MI recover to post a respectable if not especially challenging total as Rockets cruised to victory with plenty to spare.

The Hundred women's competition, Utilita Bowl

Manchester Super Giants 139-4 (100 balls): Ghosh 54 (34); Wong 2-24

Southern Brave 112-6 (100 balls): Wolvaardt 36 (28); Villiers 3-17

Manchester Super Giants won by 27 runs

Manchester Super Giants boosted their hopes of making it out of the group stage with a 27-run victory over Southern Brave.

The Super Giants had posted a competitive 139-4 after opting to make first use of the pitch in Southampton thanks to Richa Ghosh's explosive 54 off 34 balls.

Ghosh, promoted up the order to bat at three, whacked five fours and three sixes during a stand of 83 with fellow India international Smriti Mandhana who made 46 off 36 balls.

Issy Wong claimed the wickets of both players as she finished with an impressive 2-24 to stymie the momentum.

However, Brave openers Lizelle Lee (19) and Maia Bouchier (16) were unable to convert promising starts as the Super Giants' attack wrested back the initiative.

Laura Wolvaardt briefly threatened with 36 off 28 balls but when the South African was dismissed by Mady Villiers the home side's chase faltered and they ended up well short.

Villiers was the pick of the bowlers with 3-17 from her set of 20 balls as Brave lost on their own turf for the first time in this year's tournament.

The third-placed Super Giants move on to 18 points and have a six-point cushion on on Sunrisers Leeds and Welsh Fire in fourth and fifth respectively.

Charley Hull equalled the lowest round in Ladies European Tour history and broke the course record at the Centurion Club to move within one stroke of the lead at the PIF London Championship.

The English golfer fired a bogey-free 62 to climb into second place, a shot behind Canada's 17-year-old Anna Huang and breaking the lowest course mark previously set by compatriot Georgia Hall in 2021.

With her 11-under-par round, she also joined Haeran Ryu, Jessica Korda, Alison Lee, and Karrie Webb for the lowest score ever recorded on the tour.

After opening with a 74, the 30-year-old Hull made an eagle at the first hole on the second day and added nine birdies to climb up the leaderboard and finish with a 10-under total.

She said: "I have been so tired this week, exhausted from the last couple of weeks, especially after the AIG Women's Open last week.

"I feel pretty tired and my body is in bits. I have got a few ongoing injuries, so I've been having a lot of physio.

"I'm quite shocked that I've shot 11-under because I felt so tired this morning. It felt like the easiest 11-under of my life. I'm standing here right now feeling like I left a couple of shots out there and I want to go and see if I can improve it."

Hull has had an eventful week in which she defended herself following a prank she played on her caddie and finishing joint sixth in The Open after starting the final day in contention.

Wales' Lydia Hall is third on eight-under-par after her round of 67 in Hertfordshire.

Huang, who followed up her opening 67 with a 68 on Friday, said: "It was another good round, but it was a little bit more up-and-down than yesterday. I had a couple of bad mistakes here and there, but it's still something to be proud of."

title: Sullivan expected to ignore safety advice and attend West Ham game
description: David Sullivan is expected to attend Saturday's EFL Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite being advised to stay away from home matches at the London Stadium.
fullText:
West Ham are expecting David Sullivan to attend Saturday's Carabao Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth despite him being advised to stay away from home matches at London Stadium.

Sullivan, 77, resigned from his position as co-chair of West Ham in June after a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times revealed that seven women have accused Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.

He has categorically denied the allegations.

On Monday, a spokesperson for London Stadium told BBC News it had "recommended" to West Ham that Sullivan does not attend matches because of concerns about fan unrest.

London Stadium has asked for advance notice of any planned visits by major shareholder Sullivan - who retains a 38.8% stake in the club - in order to implement additional safety and operational measures.

The match against Portsmouth will be the first the club has played since the allegations against Sullivan were first reported.

The Panorama and Times joint investigation also revealed that Sullivan has been banned from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams for the past three years because of safeguarding concerns.

London Stadium was unaware of the restrictions until the BBC's report.

Sullivan was banned after a historical allegation about his conduct was raised with the Football Association in 2023. He has previously said the allegation was false.

Sullivan had already been the subject of intense fan abuse for his running of the club, who were relegated to the Championship last season for the first time since 2011.

Although West Ham have stabilised on the pitch, with key figures, including manager Nuno Espirito Santo and skipper Jarrod Bowen committing their future to the club, there remains huge uncertainty off it.

Vanessa Gold, daughter of Sullivan's late business partner and former West Ham co-chair David, backed out of a deal to sell part of her stake in the club to Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky, and instead reached an agreement with Amanda Staveley, the public face of the Saudi Arabia-backed takeover at Newcastle, to sell her entire 25.1% stake.

However, Kretinsky has since sold a small part of his own stake, bringing him under 25%.

That would allow him to buy Gold's shares under West Ham's pre-emption rights rules - which allow existing shareholders first choice to buy shares when they become available.

If he did so he would become West Ham's biggest shareholder, without triggering another clause that would force him to then buy the rest of the club.

It is anticipated Saturday's match against fellow Championship side Portsmouth (15:00 BST) will set an attendance record for an EFL Cup first-round tie, with the Hammers having sold 55,000 season tickets for the new campaign.

fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Lord's

MI London 122-9 (100 balls): Kerr 69* (41); Dean 3-26

London Spirit 119-8 (100 balls): De Klerk 35 (29); Matthews 2-21

Melie Kerr played a magnificent lone hand with the bat to keep struggling MI London's faint qualification hopes alive in the women's Hundred.

MI London, who were previously winless in five games, slumped to 23-5 and 64-8 and were on the brink of elimination to their rivals London Spirit.

But all-rounder Kerr held firm and finished with 69 not out from 41 balls to propel her side to 122-9 before the bowlers ground out a three-run win.

MI London took the confidence boost into their bowling innings and reduced Spirit to 51-4 before a stand of 42 between Nadine de Klerk and Marizanne Kapp recovered their chase.

De Klerk's departure for 35 swung the momentum back in MI London's favour as they needed 15 from six balls, and Spirit curiously promoted both Charis Pavely and Katie George above the destructive West Indies batter Deandra Dottin.

Dottin then whacked back-to-back fours to keep her side in contention but Nicola Carey held her nerve with six needed off the final ball and Spirit finished 119-8.

It completed a remarkable fightback from MI London, led by Kerr who had not hit a six in The Hundred before this innings, in which she clubbed four alongside five fours.

Kerr could only watch from the non-striker's end as Spirit captain Charlie Dean took three wickets in five balls, removing Hollie Armitage for six and Nicola Carey and Alice Monaghan without scoring.

Chinelle Henry, with 22 off 15, was the only other MI London batter to reach double figures before Kerr took 26 crucial runs from the last 10 balls including three sixes off the previously dominant Dean.

Despite the win, MI London's fate is out of their hands. They need to win both of their remaining games comfortably to boost their net run-rate and for other results to go their way, and Spirit are in the same position.

title: London submits bid for 2029 World Athletics Championships
description: London submits its final bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, with the London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics, the proposed venue.
fullText:
London has submitted its final bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships.

Athletic Ventures – a body made up of UK Athletics, London Marathon Events, and the Great Run Company – is behind the move to bring the biennial event to the capital and confirmed the final documents have been submitted to World Athletics.

London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics and used for the London Diamond League meeting for the past four years, is the proposed host venue.

The host city for the 2029 edition will be confirmed in September.

A feasibility study conducted prior to April 2025, when London's intention to bid was announced, said the competition could bring a £400m benefit to the economy, with the UK government confirming its support for the bid in July 2025.

Championship football team West Ham United, who play their home games at the London Stadium, have also offered their support for the bid.

Hodgkinson & Asher-Smith in GB squad for Europeans

London previously hosted the World Championship in 2017, while Birmingham will host the European Championships this August.

Great Run Company CEO Paul Foster hailed London as "the world's number one sporting city" while UK Athletics CEO Jack Buckner emphasised the importance of the event in the UK's "Olympic legacy".

Buckner said: "Bidding to hold the World Athletics Championships in the London Stadium, the showpiece of London 2012, was always at the centre of the UK's Olympic legacy plans.

"We are very grateful to the government, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, the Mayor of London, and UK sport for their fantastic support for this bid.

"We're delighted that we have reached agreement with the London Stadium and West Ham United for the use of the London Stadium and our sincere thanks for their commitment in making this happen."

In a statement, West Ham confirmed they are working with London Stadium LLP and Athletics Ventures to support the delivery of the Championships, with a "number of new initiatives that will enhance the stadium and matchday experience for supporters" forming part of the agreement.

The potential impact on their 2029-30 campaign if London's bid is successful is yet to be confirmed.

"Could this court produce the next NBA player? Every great player starts somewhere. Nobody starts in the NBA; they start somewhere like this."

The court in the video is the Argyle Square basketball court in Camden, London, and is the first of a pilot project under the Mayor of London's London Basketball Taskforce.

The Mayor had announced a nearly £2 million basketball investment in January 2026 before the NBA London Games, and this court program is part of that commitment.

Anunoby has become a beacon to British-born basketball players with his achievements at the highest level, winning the 2026 NBA Championship with the New York Knicks.

Anunoby averaged 16.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.6 steals in the season and 20.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals, and 1.1 blocks in the Playoffs, emerging as a fan-favorite for his relentless two-way play.

fullText:
Wayve Uber wins first minicab licence for autonomous cabs from TfL but vehicles will have a safety driver (at first)

The taxi app company Uber and the autonomous technology developer Wayve have been granted the first minicab licences in London allowing them to offer self-driving taxi rides to paying customers – but with a human safety driver in place, for now.

The companies said they would start trips in the UK “later this summer” before the full public launch.

The San Francisco-headquartered Uber and London-based Wayve are racing against the Google-owned Waymo and its Chinese equivalent Baidu’s Apollo Go to launch self-driving taxi services in London. Their progress is being watched closely because the British capital will be one of the first cities in the world to have American and Chinese tech firms operating on the same roads.

Uber and Wayve said more than 100,000 Londoners were on their waiting list for the self-driving taxis.

Transport for London (TfL), the capital’s licensing authority, granted 15 private hire vehicle licences to Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles equipped with Wayve’s artificial intelligence driving software, as well as surround cameras and radar. The companies said TfL had confirmed they reached the required safety standards.

A TfL-licensed private hire driver will sit in the driver’s seat during trips to intervene if necessary, although the software is expected to control the car.

The next step, of operating the taxis without a driver, will require Uber and Wayve to seek approval via a new process, known as an automated passenger services permit, with the government’s Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency.

TfL said it would monitor the use of the vehicles, and was ready to intervene if passenger safety was compromised. A spokesperson said: “Safety is our top priority. Any new vehicle licensed to carry passengers on London’s roads must align with our Vision Zero goal of eliminating all deaths and serious injuries from collisions on London’s streets by 2041.”

Wayve, which was co-founded by the New Zealand-born Alex Kendall, has been testing its tech in London since 2018 with safety drivers. In previous demonstrations to the Guardian the car has navigated most of the obstacles of north London’s busy roads, although the safety driver was forced to intervene at one point.

Sarah Gates, Wayve’s vice-president for global affairs and assurance, said: “This licence is an important step towards giving Londoners the chance to experience autonomous driving technology.

“The responsible deployment of these vehicles will bring us safer, cleaner and quieter streets, and we’re proud to continue working alongside regulators, communities and the public as we take the next steps towards making autonomous rides a reality in the capital.”

The licence approval was not welcomed by minicab drivers, who fear the threat to their livelihood. Matthew Wright, a regional organiser for the GMB union, raised concerns about job losses, increased unemployment and liability for accidents, and said “extreme caution” was warranted from TfL.

“This is a worrying development for our private hire driver members,” he said. “We can’t go charging ahead with new technologies without considering the implications of autonomous vehicles on all parties.”

Driverless taxi services are already operating in several cities around the world, although mainly in the US and China, where most of the software developers are based. However, US companies are essentially blocked from China, and vice versa, meaning they have not had to compete directly.

Uber abandoned its own efforts to develop self-driving technology in 2020, but it is working with several partners around the world who are in turn using different systems. That includes the Chinese company WeRide, which is operating driverless taxis in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

Wayve is also working with the Japanese manufacturer Nissan on integrating its tech in private cars.

The news came as Uber reported better than expected second-quarter gross bookings of $58.02bn (£43bn), but said earnings for the next quarter would fall below Wall Street forecasts.

The company also outlined ‌plans to spend more than $10bn on autonomous vehicles over the coming years, although it did not provide a specific ‌timeline.

title: Brilliant Brook leads Sunrisers to record Hundred score
description: Harry Brook hits a 15-ball fifty and Ryan Rickelton makes 94 not out as Sunrisers Leeds set a new Hundred record, making 241-2 against London Spirit.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Headingley

Sunrisers Leeds 241-2 (100 balls): Rickelton 94* (42), Marsh 76 (37), Brook 55 (18)

London Spirit 204-6 (100 balls): Willey 83* (46); Topley 2-30

Harry Brook shone with a sensational 15-ball fifty as Sunrisers Leeds posted the highest total in Hundred history in their 37-run win against London Spirit.

Having put in to bat at Headingley, opener Ryan Rickelton also struck 94 not out off 42 balls in Sunrisers' astonishing 241-2.

Such was the entertainment provided by Brook and the power shown by Rickelton, Mitchell Marsh's brutal 76 off 37 at the top of the order almost went unnoticed.

On a flat pitch, Marsh and Rickelton added 148 for the first wicket which gave Brook, England's limited-overs captain, the licence to go berserk.

He whacked five sixes and five fours with a combination of power and flair, including a monstrous six over mid-wicket to surpass the previous highest team total of 226.

Brook and Rickelton added 83 off 32 balls for the second wicket as Spirit's bowlers wilted, with the South African stranded short of his century as he was starved of the strike at the close of the innings.

After the carnage inflicted on their bowlers, Spirit made a disastrous start to their reply as Jonny Bairstow fell first ball to Reece Topley, and the rest of the top order also buckled under the pressure as they slipped to 44-4.

But former England all-rounder David Willey performed an admirable rescue act and saved Spirit from humiliation with 83 not out from 46 balls as the visiting side finished on 204-6.

The result takes Sunrisers to fourth in the table and keeps them in play-off contention, but leaves Spirit struggling in seventh.

Sunrisers' 241-2 surpassed Oval Invincibles 226-4 for the highest team total, which they made against Welsh Fire in 2025

Rickelton and Marsh's opening stand of 148 was the highest partnership in The Hundred, beating Jimmy Neesham and Tom Curran's 127 for Invincibles v Manchester Originals in 2023

Brook's fifty was the joint fastest in Hundred history, equalling Adam Rossington's for London Spirit against Northern Superchargers in 2022

Brook's strike rate of 305.55 was the fourth highest for a Hundred innings

Sunrisers hit 21 sixes in their innings (Marsh seven, Rickelton eight, Brook five and Dan Lawrence one). This smashes the previous Hundred record (17)

There were 31 sixes hit overall, the most in a Hundred match – beating the previous best of 29 between Birmingham Phoenix and Trent Rockets earlier this summer

The aggregate total of 445 also beat the record of 418 from that game

For Brook to outshine both Marsh and Rickelton, when the pair were so ruthlessly dominating Spirit's bowlers, indicates just how special his knock was.

Marsh kick-started the innings with his trademark ferocious strength, regularly clubbing the ball down the ground, and by the time he had reached a 24-ball half-century, Rickelton had only faced five deliveries himself.

The Australian fell with only 35 balls left in the innings but there was no respite for Spirit, as Rickelton continued to advance to his fifty off 21 balls before Yorkshire's Brook ignited the lively Headingley crowd.

Spirit's bowlers tried everything, but with no reward. When Jamie Overton perfected his wide yorker, Brook simply reached across and audaciously sliced it over deep third for six.

"That was a masterclass on how to strike the white ball," ex-England captain Michael Vaughan said on BBC Two.

"A few of Harry's shots had a bit of finesse towards the end, but it was just brute power. It's not easy for bowlers, the pitch is very flat, but London Spirit weren't on it.

"He is just brilliant. Sometimes we watch some of his innings in Test cricket and we say, 'Come on, Harry, you're better than that.'

"And we don't really give him the credit for the way that he assesses what the bowler is going to bowl to him, and he's got so many options to every delivery. He is a wonderful player."

title: “London, here I go!” – Vinicius Junior’s agent fuels Arsenal rumours with new social media post
description: Over the last few weeks, there has been increasingly speculation surrounding Vinicius Junior’s future as a Real Madrid player. With less than a year remaining on his contract, talks over a new deal ...
fullText:
Over the last few weeks, there has been increasingly speculation surrounding Vinicius Junior's future as a Real Madrid player. With less than a year remaining on his contract, talks over a new deal are set to resume soon, although there is no guarantee that a positive outcome is reached – and waiting in the wings is Arsenal.

The Premier League champions sense an opportunity to sign Vinicius, whom Real Madrid will look to sell if they cannot agree a new contract with the Brazil international. They are ready to make their move once encouragement has been given by the 26-year-old's camp, with talks having already taken place between the two parties.

And now, more negotiations are seemingly about to take place with a view to an agreement on personal terms being reached. Vinicius is represented by Roc Nation, and as per Diario AS, their president Michael Yormark posted on Instagram over the weekend that he was travelling to London, with the caption "London, here I go. Let's go!"

The emergence of Arsenal's interest has given Vinicius and his representatives leverage ahead of their showdown talks with Real Madrid. An eye-watering offer has already been tabled by last season's beaten Champions League finalists, and the likelihood is that Los Blancos will be asked to match it – or even better it – if they are to secure a renewal agreement in the coming weeks.

However, this tactic does not look like working on Real Madrid. They have already informed Vinicius' camp that the offer on the table is the best one they will get, and if it is not accepted, a sale will be sought this summer. If that happens, Arsenal would be ready to make their move, although they will have to wait until a definitive resolution comes.

title: How Mumbai Indians takeover has affected MI London & Surrey
description: BBC Sport takes a look at what has changed, what has stayed the same and what the future holds for MI London after investment from Indian Premier League side Mumbai Indians.
fullText:
The name has changed, the colours have changed and much of the conversation around the franchise has changed too.

Investment from Indian Premier League (IPL) side Mumbai Indians into Oval Invincibles led to The Hundred's most successful team rebranding itself as MI London and bringing the multi-billionaire Ambani family's cricket empire to The Oval.

Here, BBC Sport takes a look at what has changed, what has stayed the same and what the future holds for the franchise.

Reliance Industries Limited, chaired by Mukesh Ambani, bought a 49% stake in Oval Invincibles in a deal worth about £60m in January 2025, among the first sale of teams in The Hundred.

However, Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy said their relationship with India's wealthiest family began long before the bidding process got under way.

"They've been huge supporters of The Hundred for a number of years," the former South Africa cricketer told BBC Sport. "They used to take our boardroom box every August to watch The Hundred when we were still Invincibles."

Early conversations convinced Elworthy and his team they had found the right partner in the Ambanis.

"The first meeting we had, we spent about 45 minutes talking about just cricket," Elworthy said.

At about £120m, MI London are the most valuable of the franchises after their London neighbours - the Lord's-based London Spirit, who were valued at about £300m.

What has changed in The Hundred for 2026?

The Hundred 2026 - schedule and how to follow

For the investors, the attraction must have been obvious.

The Oval is one of the world's most recognisable sporting venues, Invincibles had won five titles across men's and women's competitions and Surrey regularly attracts some of the highest attendances in the county game.

"We do cricket well," Elworthy said. "We've got an incredibly strong membership, incredible attendances across formats and we are based in London. It's a really attractive proposition."

As part of the deal, Invincibles were rebranded MI London, bringing the franchise in line with the rest of the MI stable that includes MI Cape Town, MI Emirates and MI New York.

But Surrey, who remain the major shareholder, were determined not to lose their identity.

Elworthy added: "The beauty of this partnership is that the agreement was signed in late 2025 and we are halfway through our first season together, but we haven't even had to look at the contract once.

"We're only looking to make this a success together."

Not much - at least for the players, according to England all-rounder Will Jacks.

"It felt like a very smooth transition for me, having a foot in both camps," Jacks said, when asked about the team's changed identity.

The 27-year-old came through the ranks at Surrey, was part of Invincibles since its inception and also plays for MI in the IPL.

"The kit's changed obviously and it incorporates the blue and gold of MI but the training kit still has the Invincibles colours, so it is kind of a mix of the two," Jacks said.

"So I think they've done a good job of moulding the two together. But for us players and the coaching staff, everything feels very similar."

Tom Moody, who guided Invincibles to a hat-trick of men's titles as head coach, has been replaced by Kieron Pollard, who previously played in the IPL for MI as well as for their sister teams in Major League Cricket, SA20 and ILT20. Skipper Sam Billings has also left, replaced by Sam Curran.

Mitchell McClenaghan also joined from the MI network as the men's bowling coach but there is still a strong Surrey presence in the coaching staff with Gareth Batty, Jim Troughton and Nic Pothas playing prominent roles.

It's a similar story with the women's side where Lisa Keightley, fresh from coaching MI in the Women's Premier League (WPL), succeeded Jonathan Batty but is joined by Surrey women's head coach Johann Myburgh and Dan Helesfay.

Perhaps the biggest additions from the MI investment have come in the form of commercial expertise and global reach.

"MI have got teams around the world and business around the world, so that's something we've learned from them," Elworthy said.

"The Hundred previously was pretty local. Whereas now, I think we've actually got a global brand here and global partners now. That's a brilliant place to be.

"All other teams MI have around the world, they are the sole owners. But they're a minority shareholder here but we don't behave like that. We behave as a team to do the best for MI London."

Former Australia and England coach Keightley echoed Elworthy's words.

"I know MI have been very mindful that for the first time, they're working with another organisation," Keightley said. "From my experience, both organisations are working really hard to make it successful.

"MI's insight from having so many teams is definitely helpful. I know how passionate the owners are and when they commit to something, they do everything to make sure the team's successful."

For players, it also offers a chance to play for other franchises in the MI network and thereby, grow their game.

"I've been very lucky," Jacks said. "Playing with so many great players and icons of Indian cricket at MI has opened me up to a lot of new things and skills. That experience, you can't buy that."

Keightley added: "If you're a MI London player, there's definitely an opportunity to be involved in WPL. Because you build the relationship, you know what a player can do and they know the environment that they're going into."

Their supporters might still be adjusting to the new name and colours but Surrey and MI are already planning for the future.

One important part of their plans will be turning MI London into a brand that exists year-round rather than for just a few weeks each summer.

"You don't want a competition that everybody only thinks about while it's happening," Elworthy said. "It's our job to make sure there's a cycle all the way through the year."

They also plan to take greater responsibility for areas currently managed by the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB).

Having completed the takeover only months before the start of the season, they have relied on ECB to deliver operational aspects, including ticketing.

But Elworthy said the club are currently considering which services they want to take in-house from 2027.

He said: "We want to control and run all the facets of the team - the delivery of the game, the global expansion and building the brand itself."

On the field though, the ambition remains unchanged. After five titles in as many years, MI London's focus is on producing more silverware-winning teams.

That may happen very soon if their men's team can maintain the form which has seen them reach second in the table after five matches.

title: OpenUK Wants Britain to Stop Giving Away Open Source Creations
description: They point to MCP, built by two engineers in London, that ended up under US-based governance.
fullText:
OpenUK recently published its AI Openness report, and buried inside the 40-page document is a big ask from the UK government. Build Britain its own foundation that holds code, governance, and standards the way the Linux Foundation (LF) does in the US.

If you are hearing that name for the first time, OpenUK is a UK-based (obviously) non-profit that advocates for open technology and is led by Amanda Brock. They first put out this call in a report titled "Making the UK the Home of Open Source," which was submitted to UKRI earlier this year.

The AI Openness report restates the case with added urgency this time.

Characterizing the proposed British flavor of LF as a National Foundation, the body, once formed, would hold repositories, standards, and datasets built with UK public money rather than watch that work migrate to servers and governance boards based elsewhere.

It would also handle training, community engagement, and event organizing. Those are areas that would otherwise need separate infrastructure, like an open source program office (OSPO) and a sovereign fund.

OpenUK frames this as a funding and governance gap more than a technology one.

They note that the UK ranks as Europe's top country in open source software and AI openness, yet it has no equivalent to the Linux Foundation, Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency, or China's Open Atom Foundation to show for it.

The non-profit didn't have to look far to prove its point, as MCP is the group's strongest example.

The Model Context Protocol, now the standard behind how AI models connect to outside tools and data, was created by two engineers in London. Anthropic backed the protocol and eventually donated it to LF's Agentic AI Foundation, alongside Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification.

In conversation with OpenUK, David Soria Parra, one of MCP's co-creators, said that they gave MCP away because they needed the standard to stay vendor neutral, free of trademark and licensing risk.

If the UK had an established foundation, then they wouldn't have lost MCP to the US. 🙃

The European Commission has already shown off an initiative to break free from US tech dominance by moving towards an open European digital ecosystem. It would cover fields like cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, open hardware, internet technologies, and industrial applications like automotive and manufacturing.

Germany is closer to what OpenUK wants for the UK. Its Sovereign Tech Fund has turned into a government agency, and the report calls that "the right direction."

China has already proven the model works. Open source became a national pillar under its 14th Five-Year Plan, supported by a dedicated foundation called the Open Atom Foundation.

DeepSeek’s R1 showed how that focus pays off, leveraging open-weights and knowledge distillation to deliver frontier-level AI at a fraction of the cost.

OpenUK looks to garner interest from various public sector organizations across the UK while also aiming to collaborate with global experts, delivering the best proposal for their country as a result.

title: Arsenal Agree to Sell Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m After Just Seven Premier League Appearances
description:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton for a fee in the region of £7m, ending a stay in north London that lasted little more than a year and produced just seven Premier League appearances. 



 The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have reached an agreement…
fullText:
Arsenal have agreed a deal to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton for a fee in the region of £7m, ending a stay in north London that lasted little more than a year and produced just seven Premier League appearances.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have reached an agreement in principle, with Norgaard set to undergo a medical next week ahead of the move being formalised. If completed, it will bring Norgaard back into regular contact with David Moyes, who is entering his second spell in charge at Everton after replacing Sean Dyche.

Norgaard joined Arsenal from Brentford in July 2025 for a fee that could rise to £15m, arriving with a reputation built over six years as the Bees’ defensive midfield anchor and captain. He made 196 appearances for Brentford across his time at the club, taking over the captaincy from Pontus Jansson in 2023 and leading the side 68 times across all competitions.

That standing counted for little once he arrived at the Emirates. Norgaard made just seven Premier League appearances for Arsenal across the season, totalling 101 minutes on the pitch, with only one of those outings coming from the start. His final appearance in Arsenal colours came on May 24 against Crystal Palace, when he played 45 minutes in a 2-1 win. Arsenal’s central midfield had grown crowded well before Norgaard arrived, with Declan Rice established as first choice in the deepest role, Martin Zubimendi brought in from Real Sociedad for a fee that made him one of the club’s most expensive signings, and Mikel Merino also competing for minutes alongside captain Martin Odegaard further forward. Norgaard was squeezed into a squad role behind that group, used mainly to give Arteta the option of resting Rice rather than as a starter in his own right. Arsenal’s decision to cash in on Norgaard with a year still to run on his contract, rather than let him see it out on the fringes of the squad, reflects how little he featured even in a season that ended with the club lifting the Premier League title.

For Everton, the move represents a reunion between Norgaard and Moyes, and a response to a specific gap opening in the dressing room. Club captain Seamus Coleman confirmed earlier this year that his 17-year Everton career will end when his contract expires, closing out a spell in which he made 372 Premier League appearances, an Everton record, and 433 in all competitions after joining from Sligo Rovers in January 2009. Coleman announced the decision in his own words: “After more than 17 years at this great football club, I’ve decided this season will be my last as a player here.” He added a message for supporters: “I want to thank the fans for their unbelievable support. I’ve always tried my best to put Everton Football Club first and you all mean the world to me.” The club has offered Coleman the chance to stay on in a coaching capacity once he decides on the next stage of his career.

Norgaard, who has captained both Brentford and been part of Denmark squads at major tournaments, fits the profile of a player capable of filling that leadership void immediately rather than needing time to grow into it. He has won 41 caps for Denmark and featured in five matches, coming off the bench in both knockout games, as they reached the semi-finals of Euro 2020, giving him exactly the kind of tournament experience Moyes has valued in previous squads he has built.

The move would also mark Norgaard’s fourth new arrival of an Everton rebuild that has been active if unspectacular so far this summer. Moyes has already brought in Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough in a deal worth an initial £16.5m, made Tyrique George’s loan from Chelsea permanent for a fee above £20m, and signed Merlin Rohl from Freiburg for around £22m to add creativity in the final third. Alongside Coleman, Everton have also let Idrissa Gueye and Tyler Onyango leave on free transfers this summer, meaning the squad Moyes is assembling looks markedly different from the one that finished 13th last season after he returned mid-campaign to steady a club that had flirted with relegation for much of the previous four years.

With Coleman’s exit confirmed, the captaincy itself is also unresolved. Vice-captain James Tarkowski, who joined from Burnley in 2022, has made 128 appearances across all competitions and was named vice-captain in 2023 and has often led the side through Coleman’s injury spells, is widely seen as the leading contender to take over on a permanent basis, with goalkeeper Jordan Pickford and midfielder James Garner also mentioned as possible alternatives, with Garner having started every one of Everton’s 38 Premier League matches last season and led the division for combined tackles, interceptions and key passes along the way. Norgaard would not be walking into a guaranteed armband, but a player with his profile, a former club captain who led Brentford 68 times across all competitions, gives Moyes another senior voice in a dressing room losing one of its longest-serving figures.

Norgaard fits a pattern Moyes has followed throughout his career. In his second spell at West Ham, he built a side that climbed from the relegation zone to winning the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023, England’s first major trophy for the club in 43 years, largely by recruiting experienced professionals in their mid-to-late twenties rather than chasing potential. Signings like Tomas Soucek and Vladimir Coufal, who arrived together from Slavia Prague for a combined £20m, and defender Craig Dawson became central to that side not through reputation but through consistent, disciplined performances in exactly the kind of holding and defensive roles Norgaard has spent his career playing. Everton fans hoping Norgaard can offer something similar at Goodison Park have that history to point to.

The Norgaard sale is a minor deal set against the scale of Arsenal’s summer activity. The club have already reached an agreement in principle worth around €90m plus bonuses to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who has agreed personal terms on a long-term contract, while also being credited with exploring the cost of a move for Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior, as they look to build on last season’s title win, and selling fringe players like Norgaard for modest fees is a routine part of funding that kind of business. Having brought him in for up to £15m twelve months ago, recovering roughly half that outlay for a player who barely featured represents a pragmatic piece of squad management rather than a setback.

Arsenal’s spending on midfield alone last summer, capped by the Zubimendi deal, meant Norgaard was always likely to be squeezed out once he failed to force his way into Arteta’s first-choice pairing early in the season. Once a midfielder drops that far down the pecking order at a club competing on four fronts, regular football elsewhere becomes the only route back to relevance, and Everton’s £7m offer gives both parties a clean way to move on before the transfer window closes at the start of September.

At 32, Norgaard is unlikely to get many more opportunities to establish himself as a first-choice Premier League midfielder, and a move to Everton offers something Arsenal could not: regular football. His six seasons at Brentford, including the club’s first promotion to the Premier League in 74 years and the survival campaigns that followed it, showed a player who thrives on being trusted with responsibility rather than fighting for scraps of playing time behind more expensive teammates. Moyes has built his sides around experienced, disciplined midfielders in the past, and a player with Norgaard’s positional sense and leadership background suits that approach far better than it suited Arteta’s system built for tempo and press resistance in tighter areas.

Should the medical go smoothly and the transfer complete as expected, Norgaard will arrive at a club searching for exactly the profile his Arsenal spell showed he no longer suited: a captain-type figure who commands a midfield rather than watches most of a season from the bench.

For Arsenal, the deal closes a short and largely forgettable chapter. For Norgaard, it offers a route back to the regular, high-responsibility role he built his reputation on at Brentford, this time in royal blue rather than red and white stripes. Brentford supporters, who watched their former captain leave for a Premier League title winner only a year ago, will notice the irony in seeing him land at Everton rather than fighting for a starting place among the game’s biggest spenders. For Norgaard himself, the move offers something a title medal earned from the bench never could: a manager who wants him on the pitch every week.

title: Super Giants win comfortably against lowly MI
description: MI London remain without a win as Manchester Super Giants complete a comfortable six-wicket win at the Oval, while Trent Rockets hold off a late assault from Annabel Sutherland and Lauren Winfield-Hill to beat Sunrisers Leeds by five runs.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, The Oval

MI London 92 all out (99 balls): Chatli 18 (16); MacDonald-Gay 3-19

Manchester Super Giants 95-4 (72 balls): Lanning 43 (31); Gordon 2-14, Kerr 2-21

Manchester Super Giants won by six wickets

MI London remain without a win in the Hundred after Manchester Super Giants completed a comfortable six-wicket win at the Oval.

The competition's bottom side were bowled out for 92, while visiting captain Meg Lanning struck 43 as her side sealed victory with 28 balls to spare.

MI had a shocking start after being put into bat, with openers Hayley Matthews and Alice Davidson-Richards both bowled by Sophie Ecclestone for ducks.

The next four batters all reached the teens but failed to push on, while the last four MI wickets fell for five runs over the course of eight deliveries as the innings concluded with a ball to spare.

Ryana Macdonald-Gay took the final of wicket of Kirstie Gordon to finish with figures of 3-19, while Ecclestone and Maitlan Brown closed on 2-7 and 2-18 respectively.

The Super Giants opening pairing of Smriti Mandhana and Lanning took their side most of the way to their low target, putting on 73 before Mandhana was caught by Hollie Armitage off Gordon for 34.

Melie Kerr then dismissed Richa Ghosh (4) and Paige Scholfield (0) with successive deliveries, while Gordon trapped Lanning lbw with only four runs required for victory.

Mady Villiers wrapped the game up, hitting Gordon for four to condemn MI to a fourth defeat from five matches.

Third-placed Super Giants move back within two points of Trent Rockets in second, while MI remain bottom with their only points coming from a tie against London Spirit.

The Hundred women's competition, Trent Bridge

Trent Rockets 139-7 (100 balls): Dunkley 56 (33); Jonassen 2-20

Sunrisers Leeds 134-5 (100 balls): Sutherland 59* (30); Phillips 1-10

Trent Rockets held off a late assault from Annabel Sutherland and Lauren Winfield-Hill to beat defending champions Sunrisers Leeds by five runs and extend their winning streak to three matches.

Defending 139 at Trent Bridge after failing to capitalise on Sophia Dunkley's 29-ball half-century, economical bowling helped Rockets reduce Sunrisers to 76-4.

However, with 55 runs required off the final 20 balls, Sutherland dispatched Georgia Elwiss for 23 runs, including sending two full tosses away for six, to drag Sunrisers back into the match.

She and Winfield-Hill reduced the equation to 17 off five but when the latter was run out with three deliveries remaining, she took Sunrisers' hopes of victory with her.

Sutherland finished the match with a six to end unbeaten on 59 (30), with her partnership with Winfield-Hill (15) worth 50 off just 27 deliveries.

Earlier, Rockets had appeared well set for a sizeable total after Dunkley backed up her 57 against Manchester Super Giants on Friday with a knock of 56 (33), including nine fours, before being bowled by Sutherland.

Nat Sciver-Brunt and Ashleigh Gardner briefly maintained the pressure, including taking Dani Gibson's second set for 18 to carry Rockets beyond three figures off just 65 balls, but Sunrisers fought back with the ball.

Jess Jonassen and Hannah Baker took two wickets apiece as Rockets slumped from 105-2 to 118-6, with the hosts also failing to hit a boundary for 32 deliveries as their hopes of a 150-plus total faded.

A trio of fours from Bess Heath in the final set proved crucial, putting Rockets' total just out of Sunrisers' reach.

Trent Rockets' fourth victory of the tournament moves them to within four points of unbeaten Southern Brave at the top of the table. Sunrisers Leeds, who are without a win since their opener, slip to seventh.

title: Tottenham manager De Zerbi 'happy' with pre-season progress
description: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi said he was "happy for a lot of things" as they return to London unbeaten in three pre-season games after a 2-1 win over Chelsea in Sydney."I'm happy for a lot of things.
fullText:
Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi said he was "happy for a lot of things" as they return to London unbeaten in three pre-season games after a 2-1 win over Chelsea in Sydney.

The Italian spent more a week in New Zealand and Australia with his squad as he builds towards the new Premier League campaign where they aim to do better than their 17th place last season.

They head home after beating Auckland FC 2-0, recording a shootout win after a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC and a gutsy victory over their London rivals on Saturday despite playing most of the second half with 10 men.

"I'm happy for a lot of things. First of all, because we have spent a very important 10 days together. We worked very well," he said.

"I'm happy to work with these players. I'm looking forward to work with the other players who are in London -- (Rodrigo) Bentancur, Pape Matar Sarr, (Marcos) Senesi, (Mohammed) Kudus. "

Bentancur, Matar Sarr and Senesi all played at the World Cup while Kudus is recovering from an injury.

The tour gave De Zerbi an opportunity to give game time to a host of promising youngsters, as well as new signings Sandro Tonali, Andy Robertson and Marco Palestra.

He highlighted the importance of Tonali, Archie Gray, Ben Davies, Robertson and Lucas Bergvall, who all played a big part in the Chelsea victory which was sealed by Richarlison's 90th minute winner.

But the Italian also pinpointed several future prospects.

"I am so happy for the young players because Malachi (Hardy), Rio (Kyerematen), Tye (Hall), Kota (Takai), they have been in this period very important for us, very good players."

De Zerbi was particularly pleased with the way Spurs kept their composure when defender Kevin Danso was sent off for a reckless challenge three minutes into the second half against Chelsea.

He wants to see similar fight when Spurs kick off their Premier League campaign against Brentford on August 22.

"It's important to change the habits, because our habits in the last two seasons have been not good in terms of results," he said.

"It's important for us to win the game, to win the duels, to win the second ball and to play well in every position of the pitch. But yes, a very good 10 days."

Spurs play back-to-back friendlies against German side TSG Hoffenheim at home before the season starts.

fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Lord's

London Spirit 114-8 (100 balls): De Klerk 38 (28); Molineux 3-7

Southern Brave 115-5 (93 balls): Bouchier 46 (38), De Klerk 2-13, Kapp 2-16

Southern Brave won by five wickets

Leaders Southern Brave extended their unbeaten run to five matches with a five-wicket victory over London Spirit at Lord's.

Captain Sophie Molineux took 3-7 and then added 23 runs in a 52-run partnership with Maia Bouchier as Brave chased their target of 115 with seven balls to spare.

Having put Spirit into bat, Molineux struck early, removing Amy Jones (3) and Marie Kelly (0) within the space of three balls to leave the home side 10-2.

Marizanne Kapp (34) put on partnerships of 27 with opener Grace Harris (16) and Nadine de Klerk (38) but they were the only three Spirit batters to make it into double figures.

Spinners Tilly Corteen-Coleman and Sarah Glenn took two wickets apiece while Molineux returned to bowl Deandra Dottin for five as Spirit closed on 114-8.

Brave lost opener Lizelle Lee for a duck after four balls of their reply while Laura Wolvaardt and Jemimah Rodrigues fell for 13 and 12 respectively.

Bouchier pressed on, hitting a 38-ball 46 from the top of the order as she and Molineux put Brave in sight of victory, only to stumble on the line.

Both batters were dismissed with the scores level, with Bouchier stumped off the bowling of Charlie Dean and Molineux hitting the following delivery from De Klerk to Dottin, before new batter Naomi Dattani hit a winning single off her second ball.

Brave now sit eight points clear of second-placed Trent Rockets having played a game more, while Spirit remain fourth with one win, two defeats and a tie from their four matches.

The Hundred women's competition, Edgbaston

Welsh Fire 144-3 (100 balls): Voll 78 (55); Capsey 2-24

Birmingham Phoenix 145-3 (99 balls): Perry 68 (46), Capsey 51 (29); Voll 1-9

Birmingham Phoenix won by seven wickets

Ellyse Perry and Alice Capsey starred as Birmingham Phoenix picked up their first win of the women's Hundred with a nail-biting seven-wicket victory over Welsh Fire.

Chasing 145 in front of minority shareholder and England midfielder Jude Bellingham at Edgbaston, Capsey, who had earlier picked up two wickets, hit 51 (29) and Perry an unbeaten 68 (46) to help Phoenix home with one ball to spare.

Opener Davina Perrin fell just five balls into Phoenix's chase while Tammy Beaumont couldn't capitalise on being dropped on 10, picking out Heather Graham for 14, before Capsey and Perry came together for a match-changing 86-run third-wicket stand.

Capsey's dismissal, caught cheaply at deep mid-wicket by Graham off the 82nd delivery, nearly proved the turning point, with Phoenix faltering from 24 runs required from 19 balls to needing 12 runs off the final set.

But captain Perry held her nerve, trading singles with Annerie Dercksen before dispatching Graham for a six and a four to see her side over the line.

The victory – only their third in 12 matches since the beginning of the 2025 edition – moves Phoenix off the foot of the table and into fifth place after four matches. Welsh Fire slip down to seventh, with one win and three defeats.

Earlier, the tournament's leading run-scorer Georgia Voll struck a half-century for Fire against her former side, hitting nine fours and two sixes as she top-scored with 78 (55).

The Australian put on 58 for the first wicket with Ella McCaughan and a further 35 with Sophie Devine, who hit a flurry of late boundaries in her unbeaten 35 (19), but Fire were left to rue their lethargic powerplay, posting a run-a-ball 25-0.

Capsey collected 2-24 but Lauren Filer was the pick of the bowlers, conceding just 15 runs from her 20 deliveries.
