title: De Zerbi's 'ultra' roots and the Brescia connection at Spurs
description: Roberto de Zerbi says he was born an ultra, raised on the Brescia curva alongside his father - and he has carried those roots to north London.
fullText:
There is a distinctly Brescian feel to N17 of late. While the Italian city's famous old club were effectively declared bankrupt this week, a footballing passion forged at Stadio Mario Rigamonti may be fuelling Tottenham Hotspur's revival.

Roberto de Zerbi, the manager who saved Spurs from relegation last season, was raised on the terraces of Brescia's 'curva' by his father, Alfredo, who was president of the supporters' clubs. De Zerbi says he was "born an ultra".

"My dad is crazy about football. He was one of the leaders of the Brescia tifoseria. At home, we lived and breathed football. He was the one who passed that passion on to me," the Italian told Salim Lamrani in his book Football According to Roberto de Zerbi.

Tottenham's Brescia connection runs through the playing squad too. Sandro Tonali, their new record signing, joined Le Rondinelle aged 12 and made his debut as a 17-year-old, helping Brescia return to Serie A before joining AC Milan in 2020.

De Zerbi says he followed the midfielder as he rose through the ranks at his boyhood club, and Tonali told BBC Sport on Thursday about the bond they share.

"Brescia is so small. I had two weeks there and met him two or three times," he said.

"We spoke about Brescia, about the difficult situation facing our club."

However, Tonali's £100m move threatened to pose a contentious issue in Italy.

Amid mounting debt and financial problems, Brescia Calcio, owned by Massimo Cellino, were excluded from professional football by Italian authorities last summer.

They were replaced by a new team in Union Brescia, who have taken on the mantle of the city's club and play at the same iconic ground graced by Roberto Baggio and Pep Guardiola, as well as De Zerbi and Tonali.

Tonali and his wife were there to watch Union Brescia in the Serie C play-offs earlier this year - the club eventually lost to Ascoli in the final.

There were reports, however, that Cellino may look to revive Brescia Calcio in some format with the club, having trained Tonali, potentially due a percentage of his transfer fee - about £3.5m - under Fifa's solidarity contribution scheme.

But that prospect seems to have died after Brescia Calcio were wound-up in a court ruling, external on Tuesday.

As Brescia and their fans embrace a new era, the passion and footballing ethos De Zerbi learned through his father and those visits to Stadio Mario Rigamonti remain.

"Roberto's love for Brescia shaped his career," his brother, Rocco, told Corriere Della Sera.

Tonali 'took 10 minutes' to decide to join Spurs

The downfall of Brescia & rebirth in Serie C

Rosanna Pedrollo spent half a century working for Brescia, first joining the club's administration department in 1968 - she met De Zerbi's father, Alfredo, in the early 1980s through his work coordinating the supporters' clubs.

"He was always around in those days," Pedrollo tells BBC Sport. "He organised the away trips, knew which players were going to visit which supporters' clubs and when. He took care of everything.

"Alfredo was a huge football fan. He was a passionate, fiery character and a wonderful father. He was a gentle person, but full of energy at the same time. Very polite, but never afraid to say what he thought, whether people agreed with him or not.

"There aren't many people like him in football today. Everything has changed so much. He gave his passion to the club."

Pedrollo remembers a four or five-year-old De Zerbi being mascot, when he would follow the side home and away with his father. 'Roby', as his friends called him, would also watch training sessions and prepare tifos for home matches.

He happened to be a talented footballer, too, playing a stone's throw from his idols for USO Mompiano, before joining lower-league side Lumezzane and then AC Milan at the age of 12.

His father "wanted so badly" to see him play for Brescia one day, says Pedrollo, adding: "That I know for certain, because he told me many times."

Alfredo got his wish when his son spent 19 games on loan at his hometown club in 2008.

De Zerbi got his first taste for coaching in the city too, helping a friend coach youngsters at ADC Mario Rigamonti, yet many of the principles that guide his management today took root through the adversity his family faced in the economic crisis of the early '90s.

His father was forced to sell their mat factory, as well as the home De Zerbi grew up in, instead moving into a small flat.

"We had to rebuild our lives from scratch," De Zerbi told Lamrani, who says the Italian remains "true to the ideals of his youth and to his working-class roots".

Indeed, the day after signing his first professional contract with Milan, De Zerbi says he was at the bank signing a mortgage to buy his parents a house.

"Coming from a modest background, success has never led him to abandon his principles or his values," adds Lamrani, who also worked as Marcelo Bielsa's disciplinary coach and interpreter at Leeds United.

"He has preserved the principles of solidarity and generosity instilled in him by his parents and has never renounced his social origins. He knows exactly which side of the barricades he stands on: with the people.

"He instinctively sides with the oppressed. That reflects his rebellious temperament, forged by his own life story."

Lamrani says De Zerbi "remains deeply attached to the people on the terraces" - and to his Brescian roots. That was obvious when Marseille welcomed Atalanta in the Champions League last season.

George Boxall, author of FADA! A Season in Marseille, who followed De Zerbi's time in France, recalls the Italian performing the famous Brescia 'V' sign towards the away end.

"I was born in Brescia, a hundred metres from the stadium; I'm a Brescia tifoso - it's in my family's DNA - and for us, playing Atalanta is like a fiercely contested derby; we'd be thinking about it from Monday to Sunday," said De Zerbi at the time.

"Roberto is a man of the terraces, a man of the people: straightforward, loyal and authentic," adds Lamrani.

"He loves terrace culture, particularly at working-class clubs such as OM. He grew up on the streets and absorbed their unwritten codes. For him, a person's word is sacred.

"He is generous by nature, giving of himself without reserve and trusting his instincts. He has little patience for selfishness or opportunism. That outlook is deeply rooted in ultra culture."

title: Ultra-rich are buying up $49 million mansions in London, with ‘Trump unease’ generating a 10% rise in Americans investing in Britain
description: In the first half of this year, Americans accounted for 30% of London’s luxury home sales above $20 million. A real estate expert blames unease over Trump.
fullText:
Wealthy Americans are swapping U.S. ZIP codes for foreign postcodes, chasing stability as the U.S. grapples with a soaring cost-of-living, political polarization, and economic uncertainty. And now, they're snapping up prime real estate in one of the world's most expensive housing markets: London.

The British capital has witnessed a staggering jump in the number of sales valued above £15 million ($20 million)—and it's largely being driven by Americans with deep pockets, according to luxury real estate company Beauchamp Estates.

Who are the typical American buyers in London's market?

Why are wealthy Americans buying luxury London real estate?

What factors are driving American emigration from the US?

How much has London's luxury property market grown?

An estimated £1.24 billion ($1.66 billion) worth of property was sold across 34 deals between January and June of this year, compared to the £694.1 million ($928 million) sales across 27 properties in the same period of 2025. The average sales price hit £36.5 million ($48.8 million), a £10.8 million rise ($14.5 million) from the year before.

And in the first half of this year, Americans accounted for 30% of all home sales above $20 million—up from 20% at the end of 2025—helping fuel the £546 million ($730 million) rise within just six months.

The average U.S. buyer of London's high-class properties are usually young couples in their 30s to mid-50s, who have one of two young children. And Beauchamp Estates notes an influx of wealthy AI and tech coming in from across the pond; since the start of 2026, there has been a 10% rise in wealthy Americans working in the sectors acquiring top-tier London homes.

Now, ultra-rich U.S. expats are making the move to the U.K. cultural hub to dodge America's political tension and soaring living costs.

There are reasons behind why they're picking the cobblestone streets of London over the white-sand beaches of California. The real estate firm says that newly minted tech wealth, favorable buying conditions, and uncertainty surrounding the Trump administration are driving more Americans to the city's luxury housing market.

"The U.S. economy and booming tech sector are generating significant wealth, but unease over Trump has helped to generate a 10% rise in American buyers transferring some of their money offshore into London property purchases," Rosy Khalastchy, the director and head of St John's Wood Office at Beauchamp Estates, said in a press release shared with Fortune.

Industries like private equity, tech, and AI are fueling a billionaire boom. The world gained around two million new millionaires last year—the biggest jump in five years—and the soaring value of AI companies acted as "primary engine" of wealth gains, according to a 2026 report from consulting firm Capgemini. And with London real estate prices more than 20% below their 2014 peak, buyers can now get more bang for their buck. Beauchamp Estates also points to a preferential exchange rate, opportunities for deals and discounts, and the city being viewed as "a good European business base" to grow their success. And beyond the financial incentives, Americans are choosing London for its social scene and quality education system.

title: Raids across UK in crackdown on nuisance car finance texts
description:
Laptops, phones and documents seized as information commissioner acts on messages about mis-selling scandal
Laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized after officials carried out search warrants in a crackdown on claims companies plaguing people with spam text messages about the car finance mis-selling scandal.
The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) executed warrants at homes and businesses linked to five companies in London, Liverpool, Bolton, Burnley and Swansea on Wednesday.

fullText:
Laptops, phones and documents seized as information commissioner acts on messages about mis-selling scandal

Laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized after officials carried out search warrants in a crackdown on claims companies plaguing people with spam text messages about the car finance mis-selling scandal.

The UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) executed warrants at homes and businesses linked to five companies in London, Liverpool, Bolton, Burnley and Swansea on Wednesday.

More than 12m complaints about nuisance marketing text messages have been submitted by the public since September 2025 as claims management companies (CMCs) and other firms attempt to grab a share of the billions of pounds in compensation expected to be paid out to motorists who were mis-sold car loans.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced a £7.5bn industry-wide compensation scheme for the millions of victims of the scandal in March.

Legal challenges, however, forced the regulator to partly suspend the scheme.

The FCA had expected to start paying out £829 on average this year to those affected by the scandal – in which drivers were overcharged for loans as a result of commission payments between lenders and car dealers between 2007 and 2024 – but a court ordered the regulator to suspend parts of the scheme until a hearing in December or February next year.

The head of investigations at the ICO, Andy Curry, said: “People are fed up with being bombarded by unwanted calls, texts and emails about car finance claims, and we’re taking action.”

This week’s raids “send a clear message to the claims management sector: comply with the law or expect to hear from us”, he said.

The companies linked to the searches are subject to continuing investigation. They are believed to be responsible for sending a combined 170m texts to members of the public between September 2025 and May this year.

The ICO is working with the FCA, the Advertising Standards Authority and the Solicitors Regulation Authority to tackle poor practices relating to motor finance claims by some CMCs, law firms and lead generation companies.

The raids represent an escalation of the crackdown on rogue CMCs and other businesses. As a result of the FCA’s work, more than 1,200 misleading adverts have been removed or amended since January 2024.

Some firms face enforcement investigations, while others have had to reduce their “unreasonable” fees or allow consumers to walk away from contracts free of charge.

The ICO has the power to apply to the courts for a warrant to search premises as part of investigations under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations, where evidence may be seized. This can include mobile phones, laptops and sim farms: collections of devices that house hundreds or thousands of mobile phone sim cards.

The FCA has said there is no need to use a CMC or law firm because people can complain for free using a template letter on its website. This week it launched a nationwide advertising campaign to direct people to the letter. It will run across TV, radio, print, billboards and social media until 6 September.

title: London City host Man Utd to kick off WSL season
description: London City Lionesses are handed a Women's Super League opener against Manchester United as the Women's Super League fixtures are announced.
fullText:
Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas is set to make her London City Lionesses' debut against Manchester United when the Women's Super League season kicks off.

London City will host United in the opening match of the 2026-27 WSL season on Friday, 4 September (19:00 BST).

Spain midfielder Putellas is the highest profile of the eight signings made by Eder Maestre.

His ambitious side face a United team hoping to bounce back after failing to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The BBC will broadcast 25 matches during the campaign, beginning with eight-time champions Chelsea taking on Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, 5 September (12:30 BST), live on BBC One.

The Blues will play all of their home league matches at the main stadium this year, ending a nine-year stay at Kingsmeadow.

On the season's first Sunday, defending champions Manchester City begin their campaign at home against promoted Birmingham City while Tottenham host West Ham United.

Charlton Athletic and Crystal Palace, also promoted from the WSL 2 as the English top flight expands to 14 teams, will host Liverpool and Everton respectively.

Finally, title hopefuls Arsenal return to Brighton where a 1-1 draw in May ensured Manchester City won the 2025-26 Women's Super League.

Full list of 2026-27 Women's Super League fixtures

Man City crowned WSL champions after Arsenal held at Brighton

What's working - and what's not - for WSL fans?

Last season's top three will all face each other before the end of November.

Chelsea host Arsenal on 27 September with the Gunners travelling to Etihad Stadium to play Manchester City a week later on 4 October.

Andree Jeglertz's side are scheduled to go to Stamford Bridge on 14 November, a game that will be live on the BBC.

Also on the BBC will be Manchester United's derby games against Liverpool and Manchester City (currently 4 and 25 October respectively).

Last season, most WSL matches took place at 12:00 on Sundays, a time that was not universally popular given its clash with grassroots fixtures.

For 2026-27, the schedule is more varied, with more games planned for Friday evenings, as well as Saturday lunchtime fixtures and matches staggered across Sunday afternoons, including the return of an evening fixture on certain weeks.

On Tuesday, the WSL released details of its new Players Cup, formerly the League Cup, and the BBC will show March's final in full, as well as numerous matches from the Women's Champions League - including the final - throughout the season.

The campaign will culminate with the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil and the BBC will bring extensive coverage of the game's biggest event.

All eyes will be on Putellas' debut in the WSL - and London City have hit the jackpot with a home opener against a United team many believe they can topple this season.

They will want to capitalise on that opportunity to bring in supporters and grow the fanbase - with Putellas, among other star signings including ex-Manchester United goalkeeper Mary Earps, set to be the face of that opening fixture.

It is a tough start for United, who take on London City, Chelsea and Arsenal in their first three games - a run that could show whether they can challenge for the title or are in shape to secure a Champions League spot.

In contrast, champions Manchester City will be pleased with their start, avoiding their closest rivals until October, meaning they could have the chance to open up a lead at the top.

Newcomers Charlton Athletic will play their first ever WSL fixture at home, which is sure to be a great occasion for the club.

The match between Birmingham City and Crystal Palace in September – last season's WSL 2 top two – could be another key one in the calendar.

The big derby matches taking place in February and March always carry intriguing storylines, while the expansion of the league means there is an additional game for fans to watch each weekend.

Naturally, when European competition kicks in, there is scope for the calendar to shuffle around a little but clubs now have an idea of where their tricky spells could occur this season.

title: FTSE 100 hits record high despite AI sell-off
description:
Strong corporate results buoy market as investors move money away from tech and semiconductor stocks 
London’s FTSE 100 stock index has touched a fresh high, driven by strong corporate results as investors moved money away from tech and semiconductor stocks amid the global tech stock sell-off.
The UK’s blue chip index rose as high as 10,951 points on Wednesday morning before falling back slightly, its best level since 27 February, the day before the US and Israel began attacks on Iran and sparked stock market volatility.

fullText:
Strong corporate results buoy market as investors move money away from tech and semiconductor stocks

London’s FTSE 100 stock index has touched a fresh high, driven by strong corporate results as investors moved money away from tech and semiconductor stocks amid the global tech stock sell-off.

The UK’s blue chip index rose as high as 10,951 points on Wednesday morning before falling back slightly, its best level since 27 February, the day before the US and Israel began attacks on Iran and sparked stock market volatility.

On a day of fresh losses for the tech-heavy Nasdaq index, the FTSE 100 closed up 0.3% at 10,908, marginally below its record closing value of 10,910 in February.

The FTSE 100 is heavily weighted towards the finance and energy sectors, meaning it has been largely shielded from the sell-off in tech stocks that has rattled other global markets, particularly in Asia and New York.

The Asia-focused bank Standard Chartered and the miner Rio Tinto both announced a rise in shareholder payouts on Wednesday.

The FTSE 100’s climb came as shares in companies linked to AI plunged for the second day in a row over concerns about spending on the technology, sending stock markets in South Korea and Japan tumbling.

The oil price continued to climb after the US military said it had knocked down an Iranian missile barrage and worked with Saudi Arabia’s forces to strike sites in Iraq that Tehran-backed militias had recently used to launch attacks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose above $90 a barrel by late afternoon in London, a rise of more than 7%.

Seoul’s Kospi index is dominated by semiconductor manufacturers, and disappointing results from the chipmaker SK Hynix left it down by as much as 12.6% at one point before it rebounded.

The index closed down 6% after falling almost 11% the previous day, reaching its lowest level since early April and marking an almost 40% fall from the peak reached a little over a month ago.

Trading was halted for 20 minutes for the second consecutive session after an 8% plunge triggered a market-wide circuit breaker.

Japan’s Nikkei also closed 1.5% down on Wednesday, a two-month low.

SK Hynix, which produces the chips essential to the expansion of AI datacentres, reported record profits for the second quarter but undershot investors’ expectations.

That prompted a sell-off that drove its shares down by as much as 20% before they recovered to 10% down. Shares in its fellow chipmaker Samsung Electronics also tumbled further, closing 5% lower.

The two companies together account for more than half of the market capitalisation of the Kospi, which has led to them holding sway over the market this year. The companies have brought in cash from investors looking to become involved in the lucrative AI trade amid a global shortage of advanced memory chips.

Analysts said disappointment over SK Hynix’s earnings highlighted investors’ concerns about how long tech companies could continue their spending spree on the technology.

“SK Hynix delivered strong results, but in today’s AI market strong is ‌no longer enough,” said Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments in Singapore.

“Investors were looking for additional catalysts, particularly around long-term agreements and shareholder returns, to support a memory sector that has become the epicentre of the AI trade.”

Shares in US chip companies fell on Wall Street on Tuesday. Intel, Advanced Micro Devices, Sandisk, Western Digital Corp and Seagate Technology were all down.

Apple benefited from the falls as investors losing confidence in AI stocks sought a safe haven. Its shares briefly rose above the $5tn (£3.76tn) valuation mark, only the second company ever to do so.

Shares in Taiwan’s TSMC, the world’s largest contract chipmaker, fell 3% on Wednesday in Taipei.

Analysts said small-time investors had led the charge on buying chipmakers’ stocks, many using borrowed money. While this pushed stocks higher in last month’s rally, it has worsened the sell-off as many have pulled their money out.

South Korea’s finance minister, Koo Yun-cheol, told the national assembly the government was reviewing market stabilisation measures.

The broker AJ Bell’s investment director, Russ Mould, said the FTSE 100 had been “helped by its lack of exposure to technology and AI stocks, and a slew of strong corporate results, with index heavyweights Standard Chartered, Reckitt Benckiser and Rio Tinto all delivering either better-than-expected profits, or bumper cash returns to shareholders, or both”.

title: Pretorius drives Spirit to win over MI London
description: Lhuan-dre Pretorius recovers from a heavy collision in the field to hit 64 as London Spirit beat MI London by seven wickets for their first win in this season's Hundred.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, The Oval

MI London 164-5 (100 balls): Jacks 65 (44); Overton 3-30

London Spirit 165-3 (89 balls): Pretorius 64 (28); Gleeson 1-23

London Spirit won by seven wickets

Lhuan-dre Pretorius recovered from a heavy collision in the field to hit 64 as London Spirit beat MI London by seven wickets for their first win in this season's Hundred.

The South African and James Coles ran into one another chasing a catch late in the first innings, in which reach MI London reached 164-5.

Pretorius left the field after the incident but was fit to open the Spirit innings and hit three fours and seven sixes in his 28-ball innings, which started with a 63-run partnership with Jonny Bairstow (23).

The 20-year-old added a further 38 with Liam Livingstone (16) before he was caught by Sherfane Rutherford off the bowling of Richard Gleeson.

James Rew (19) and Dewald Brevis (37 from 18) finished the job off for Spirit, who won with 11 balls to spare.

MI London had started well after being put into bat, with Will Jacks (65) and James Vince (26) putting on a 91-run opening partnership.

However both openers and Nicholas Pooran fell in the space of eight balls as the home side slipped to 100-3.

Both Jacks and Pooran were dismissed by Jamie Overton, who later removed Jason Roy (13) for figures of 3-30.

Rutherford accelerated at the close for MI, striking a 19-ball 41 that featured four sixes before he was caught by Coles off Andrew Tye from the last ball of the innings.

Spirit move into sixth, above Southern Brave and Birmingham Phoenix, after claiming their first win in three matches, while MI London sit in fourth with two wins and two defeats.

title: MI London hold out in nail-biting tie with Spirit
description: MI London hold London Spirit to a nail-biting tie at The Oval after Hayley Matthews concedes only three runs from the last three balls of the match.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, The Oval

MI London 151-4 (100 balls): Kerr 49* (32); Kapp 2-24

London Spirit (151-5 balls): Jones (49); Gordon 2-29, Matthews 2-33

MI London held London Spirit to a nail-biting tie at The Oval after Hayley Matthews conceded only three runs from the last three balls of the match.

With Spirit needing nine off the final set, Matthews' international team-mate Deandra Dottin struck a four off the first ball before adding a single from the following delivery.

Matthews struck back, having Nadine de Klerk caught at deep mid-wicket for 13 and keeping new batter Charlie Dean to a single.

Dottin was only able to chop Matthews' final delivery into the leg side, scrambling through for two as the two sides played out their second tie in three years.

The south London franchise, who secured their first points of the season after losing their opening three matches, reached 151-4 after being put into bat.

Melie Kerr struck an unbeaten 49 from 32 balls from number three, putting on 46 with captain Hollie Armitage (23) and an unbroken stand of 54 with Chinelle Henry, who hit two fours and two sixes in a 12-ball 33.

Henry then had big-hitting opener Grace Harris caught by Armitage off the first ball of the reply, but Amy Jones steadied the Spirit innings.

The visiting wicketkeeper also top-scored with 49, with her total coming from 36 balls, putting on partnerships of 68 with Marie Kelly (45) and 51 with Marizanne Kapp (25).

Spirit looked well set, needing 33 from 26 balls, before they lost Jones and Kapp within the space of four deliveries.

Kapp top-edged Matthews to Dani Gregory immediately after hitting a six, while Jones swept Kirstie Gordon to Nicola Carey at backward square straight after hitting four through the covers.

MI kept themselves in the hunt, conceding 19 off the next 17 balls, setting up the dramatic final set which saw Spirit finish on 151-5.

The home side move off the bottom of the table, with their two points taking them above Birmingham Phoenix on net run-rate.

Spirit rise above Welsh Fire and Sunrisers Leeds to sit fourth, with a win, a defeat and a tie from their three matches.

Jurrien Timber has travelled back to London from Arsenal's training camp in Spain in a move related to the groin injury that caused him to miss the end of last season.

The Netherlands international missed two months towards the end of last season because of an ankle injury, but returned in time for the Champions League final loss to Paris St-Germain.

However, a groin issue then caused him to miss the World Cup.

It is now understood that the right-back has returned to London from the Gunners' training camp in Spain but sources insist the visit is part of his rehabilitation schedule and not because of a setback in his recovery.

Timber is expected to return to Spain to rejoin the squad.

Timber, the Gunners' first-choice right-back, played 30 Premier League games as they won the title last season.

He joined Arsenal from Ajax in July 2023 for an initial fee of £34m, but missed most of his first season after tearing his anterior cruciate knee ligament.

title: China in touch with Yemen's Houthis to allow ships to sail through Red Sea, sources say
description: , Parisa Hafezi, Timour Azhari and Chen Aizhu LONDON/DUBAI, July 28 (Reuters) - China has held direct talks with Yemen's Houthi movement to enable its tankers to sail through the
fullText:
LONDON/DUBAI, July 28 (Reuters) - China has held direct talks with Yemen's Houthi movement to enable its tankers to sail through the southern Red Sea without being attacked after the Iran-aligned militia ‌pledged to prevent access to Saudi ports, six sources with knowledge of the matter have said.

The Houthis declared their blockade ‌on July 20, opening a new front against the U.S. and its allies in the Iran war and expanding attacks on tankers carrying energy and other supplies to markets ​beyond the Middle East.

Beijing has asked the Houthis directly to promise safe passage for its tankers, according to the sources, who included a senior Iranian official.

China was among the first countries to contact the Houthis directly about transits through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea with Yemen on its eastern bank, said the sources, who declined to be identified due to the sensitivity of the matter.

CHINA CLEARS VESSELS INDIVIDUALLY ‌WITH HOUTHIS, SOURCES SAY

Beijing is seeking to keep ⁠oil exports flowing from Saudi Arabia's Red Sea terminals, principally Yanbu, to help plug the gap in supplies caused by Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the exit from the Gulf.

China's transport ministry, the ⁠Houthis' media office and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

At least four tankers have loaded crude from Saudi ports bound for China and transited Bab el-Mandeb since the Houthis announced their restrictions, according to Kpler analysis and LSEG and MarineTraffic ship tracking data.

Chinese officials have cleared each ​vessel ​individually with the Houthis, one of the sources said, and both sides have ​informed Iran of their actions, two officials in the region ‌briefed by Tehran told Reuters.

The Houthis have told international shipping companies in an email that vessels may be attacked if they load or discharge cargo at Saudi Arabian ports.

Some tankers trying to enter the Red Sea through the Bab el-Mandeb have changed course because of safety worries, two separate Chinese trade sources said.

TWO TANKERS CHANGE COURSE TO AVOID STRAIT

The New Champion and New Prime oil supertankers both sailed back out of the Gulf of Aden into open waters, according to analysis from Lloyd's List Intelligence and MarineTraffic ship tracking data.

The New Champion had been due ‌to call at Yanbu to load oil, while the New Prime was already ​loaded with oil, according to Kpler and other industry data and ship tracking.

The two ​vessels' operator, Hong Kong-based Associated Maritime, did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.

The Houthis said last week they had carried out missile and drone strikes on two ‌Saudi oil tankers, the Encelia and the Layla. Maritime security ​sources confirmed the strike on the ​Encelia, though Reuters could not immediately confirm the attack on the Layla.

Sailing southward from Yanbu to Asia through Bab el-Mandeb takes on average 16 days. If the ship turns north for the Suez Canal and then sails west and south around Africa, it ​takes 50 days.

The Houthis have maintained good relations ‌with China and there has been close coordination in the past between them, especially on oil shipments to China from ​Saudi Arabia, two sources close to the Houthis told Reuters.

title: Jacks hits fifty as MI London seal last-ball win
description: Will Jacks hits his first half-century of this year's edition of The Hundred as MI London claim a nerve-shredding last-ball victory over Southern Brave.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Utilita Bowl

Southern Brave 129-9 (100 balls): Smith 49 (26); Boult 2-15

MI London 130-7 (100 balls): Jacks 54 (41); Stoinis 3-17

Will Jacks hit his first half-century of this year's edition of The Hundred to help MI London claim a nerve-shredding last-ball win over Southern Brave.

Jacks hit three fours and two sixes in his 41-ball knock of 54 to provide the backbone of MI's chase of 130 on a tricky pitch in Southampton.

At 93-3 and with England all-rounder Jacks in good touch, MI had looked on course for a comfortable win only to lose four wickets for 34 runs.

The momentum shifted to Brave when Jacks was trapped lbw to a toe-crushing yorker from Marcus Stoinis, who had earlier removed MI skipper James Vince and Nicholas Pooran for ducks in consecutive deliveries.

Sherfane Rutherford's 21 off 12 balls swung it back the visitors' way only for a nail-biting finale as he and Rashid Khan were run out while Tom Curran was bowled by Nikhil Chaudhary.

With two runs needed from the final delivery of the match - bowled by Chaudhary - Ollie Pope managed to slash through point and scamper back for a second.

Brave had earlier posted 129-9 thanks to a 26-ball 49 from England wicketkeeper Jamie Smith at the top of the order.

Smith cracked six fours and two sixes before he chipped a slower ball from veteran seamer Richard Gleeson into the hands of long on.

Tristan Stubbs added 38 off 31 balls while Chaudhary made 13, but they were the only other Brave players to make double figures.

The wickets were shared around MI's attack with Kiwi left-arm seamer Trent Boult the pick with 2-15 as Tom Curran, Sam Curran and Gleeson also claimed two apiece.

MI are third in the standings on eight points - level with leaders Manchester Super Giants and second-placed Welsh Fire having played a game more - while Brave are second bottom having lost their first three games.

The focus switches to Headingley in The Hundred on Tuesday, where Sunrisers Leeds host Manchester Super Giants in a double header.

description: Lauren Bell holds her nerve as Southern Brave win a last-ball thriller against MI London to maintain their 100% start to this year's edition of The Hundred.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Utilita Bowl

Southern Brave 126-7 (100 balls): Wolvaardt 35 (30); Matthews 4-22

MI London 125-3 (100 balls): Wyatt-Hodge 52* (42); Wong 1-20

Lauren Bell held her nerve as Southern Brave won a last-ball thriller against MI London to maintain their 100% start to this year's edition of The Hundred.

With eight runs required off the final five deliveries of the match, Bell kept her cool as MI fell one run short of Brave's total of 126-7.

Danni Wyatt-Hodge had laid the foundation for MI's chase with an unbeaten half-century, but with four needed off Bell's final delivery she was unable to find a boundary.

Bell was mobbed by her Brave team-mates as they made it three wins from their opening three fixtures to remain top of the standings while winless MI were left to rue how they made such a hash of the chase.

Earlier, Maia Bouchier had given Brave's innings some early impetus with a breezy 31 off 22 balls before she was caught slog-sweeping Hayley Matthews to deep mid-wicket.

South Africa batter Laura Wolvaardt then shared a 60-run stand for the third wicket with the more fluent Jemimah Rodrigues, who made 32 off 22 deliveries only to be snared by Matthews.

But Brave's innings faded away towards the end in the face of some tight bowling from MI as Matthews finished with 4-22.

West Indies all-rounder Matthews then gave MI a solid platform in the chase, smacking four fours in her 32 off 28 deliveries only to miss a straight one from Issy Wong.

Wyatt-Hodge and MI skipper Holly Armitage looked to have things under control only for the latter to depart for 27 after feathering an edge off Sarah Glenn into the gloves of Lizelle Lee.

MI then struggled to find the middle of the bat as Wong and Sophie Molineux bowled tightly to ramp up the pressure further.

Victory still appeared within reach for MI when Bell stepped up to bowl the final set for Brave, but neither Wyatt-Hodge nor Nicola Carey could find the clean strike required to beat the fielders as they fell agonisingly short.

title: De Klerk holds nerve as Spirit edge past Rockets
description: South African all-rounder Nadine de Klerk stars with 41 not out from 22 balls as London Spirit beat Trent Rockets with three balls to spare.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Trent Bridge

Trent Rockets 142-7 (100 balls): Gardner 34 (22); Kapp 3-12

London Spirit 146-5 (97 balls): De Klerk 41* (22); Gardner 2-24

London Spirit won by five wickets

All-rounder Nadine de Klerk held her nerve to lead London Spirit to a tense five-wicket win over Trent Rockets with three balls to spare.

Chasing 143 at Trent Bridge, Spirit were in trouble at 67-4 after losing four wickets for 12 runs and were in danger of wasting their positive start from opener Grace Harris' knock of 37 from 20 balls.

But De Klerk and Marie Kelly combined for a counter-attacking stand of 63 from 37 balls to propel Spirit to their first win of the season.

With power-hitter Deandra Dottin waiting in the dugout, there was some concern about Kelly's slow start as she stuttered to 12 from 13 balls, but she impressively kicked on to score 39 from 26 deliveries.

After her departure with 13 still needed to win, Rockets' bowlers fought to take the game deep but De Klerk - who has made a name for herself as a finisher in the past couple of years - whacked two sixes in the last four balls in a nerveless knock of 41 not out from 22 balls.

Earlier, De Klerk's fellow South African Marizanne Kapp had set the tone with the ball for Spirit with a fine spell of 3-12.

Kapp bowled Beth Mooney first ball before removing Sophia Dunkley and Sophie Luff, but Ash Gardner's 34 and a dynamic 31 off 19 balls from Bess Heath led Rockets' recovery to 142-7.

Gardner was caught on the boundary off England's Charlie Dean, who also impressed with 2-18, which allowed Spirit to keep the run-rate under control as Heath struggled for support from the lower order.

Both teams have one win from two so far, but Rockets are more comfortable at third in the table with a superior net run-rate.

title: Devine inspires Fire to dominant win over MI London
description: MI London remain winless in the women's Hundred after a 60-run thrashing by Welsh Fire, while Southern Brave beat Sunrisers Leeds for back-to-back wins.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Sophia Gardens

Welsh Fire 177-4 (100 balls): Devine 52 (29); Matthews 2-52

MI London 117 (92 balls): Henry 30 (23); Potts 3-24

An impressive Welsh Fire earned their first win of the women's Hundred with a 60-run thrashing of MI London in Cardiff.

Fire suffered a poor defeat by Southern Brave in their opener but bounced back to post 177-4, comfortably the highest total in the tournament so far this year and the third-highest in its history.

After openers Ella McCaughan and Georgia Voll added 49, captain Sophie Devine and all-rounder Georgia Wareham added 79 from just 35 balls for the fourth wicket as MI London's bowlers wilted.

Devine was stumped from the penultimate ball for 52 from just 29 balls including four sixes, one of which was smacked out of the ground, while Wareham finished unbeaten on 43 from 20.

To conclude the entertaining innings, Em Arlott came out with one ball to face and launched it for six, as Fire's performance provided much-needed entertainment for the women's tournament where the previous highest team total so far was just 126.

In reply, MI London - despite a batting line-up stacked with international quality - crumbled to 117 all out and suffered their second successive defeat.

Fire seamer Grace Potts dominated the powerplay with figures of 3-24 as MI London crumbled under the run-rate pressure. Potts accounted for MI London's powerful top three of Hayley Matthews for 10, Danni Wyatt-Hodge for 12 and Kira Chathli for two.

Devine backed up her knock with figures of 2-15, including the wicket of Chinelle Henry who was MI London's top-scorer with 30, while Welsh left-arm spinner Sophia Smale chipped in with 2-17.

MI London will take on unbeaten Southern Brave on Monday as they search for their first win, while Fire face Trent Rockets on Wednesday.

The Hundred women's competition, Headingley

Sunrisers Leeds 116 all out (100 balls): Smith 48 (34); Wong 3-15

Southern Brave 117-5 (96 balls): Rodrigues 42* (34); McCarthy 2-14

Southern Brave won by five wickets

In the earlier women's match, Jemimah Rodrigues struck an unbeaten 42 to guide Southern Brave to a five-wicket victory against Sunrisers Leeds and maintain their perfect start to The Hundred.

The Indian batter, who played a starring role in her country's maiden ODI World Cup triumph last year, helped Brave recover from a difficult start to their chase of 117 and hit the winning runs with four balls to spare.

It was the Brave's second win from as many matches in the women's competition.

Sunrisers pacer Cassidy McCarthy had removed both Lizelle Lee and Maia Bouchier with superb inswingers, while South Africa skipper Laura Wolvaardt also fell cheaply as Brave fell to 36-3 after 40 balls at Headingley.

But Rodrigues partnered with captain Sophie Molineux (21) to steady their innings before finding crucial boundaries in the closing stages to wrap up the win.

Earlier, Bryony Smith scored 48 from 34 balls for Sunrisers, but Issy Wong claimed 3-15 and Tilly Corteen-Coleman registered 2-25 to keep their scoring in check.

Sunrisers looked well set at 78-2 but lost eight wickets in adding the final 38 runs, suffering a dramatic collapse to be bowled out for 116 - a total that proved difficult to defend.

title: Beaugrand and Hauser take London triathlon wins as GB miss out
description: Cassandre Beaugrand and Matt Hauser claim their third win of this year's World Triathlon Championship Series.
fullText:
Cassandre Beaugrand and Matt Hauser both claimed a third win in this year's World Triathlon Championship Series in London, where British hopes were hindered by crashes on the bike.

Tilly Anema was unable to continue after hitting a cone while part of a lead duo, while fellow Briton Alex Yee was a minute down on a 13-man lead group before he got tangled up in a crash shortly before the second transition.

Olympic champion Yee produced the quickest time for the run - his strongest discipline - but that gained only 17 seconds on Hauser and Vasco Vilaca, who put on a thrilling sprint finish in the men's race.

World champion Hauser won in 50 minutes 28 seconds, with Portugal's Vilaca three seconds behind the Australian on a course consisting of a 750m swim, 20km bike ride and 5km run.

Hungary's Csongor Lehmann was third - eight seconds behind Hauser - while Yee was more than a minute back in 14th and compatriot Max Stapley 12th.

Olympic champion Beaugrand won the women's race in 56mins 6secs, five seconds ahead of Germany's Lisa Tertsch, with Sweden's Tilda Mansson 15 seconds adrift.

Beth Potter and Georgia Taylor-Brown were the best-placed Britons in fourth and sixth respectively as London hosted the WTCS for the first time since 2015.

Beaugrand was 27th out of the water but stayed safe in the chase group on the bike before hitting the front on the run, holding off a late challenge from world champion Tertsch.

"I had one of my worst swims ever," Beaugrand said. "I had to wake up on the bike and tried to save some energy for the run."

With two more races before the grand final, Potter still leads the women's rankings - Beaugrand is sixth - while Vilaca is the men's leader with Hauser third.

Both Vilaca and Hauser were in the lead group throughout, before Hauser pulled clear around the final two corners.

"It was nice to have another battle with Vasco and see what we had left at the end," said Hauser.

With NATO's European members and ​Canada sharply increasing defence spending, U.S. companies argue it is faster and cheaper to buy proven American systems than develop new ones, while pledging to localise production and technology.

At Farnborough, Lockheed announced a lower-cost Patriot interceptor to be developed with European and U.S. partners. It comes shortly after an announcement about plans to produce an Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) with Germany's Rheinmetall. RTX's Raytheon also recently announced it had partnered with European firms to increase Stinger missile production, including assembly in the Netherlands.

Europeans benefit from systems that are ‌widely used, such as the Patriot, where the many countries ⁠using it pool funding to support features such as a threat database, said Thomas Laliberty, president of Raytheon's land and air defence systems. "They get a lot of benefit from that collective," he said.

Newer defence-tech firms are also making a push. Anduril, which had ⁠a major presence at Farnborough for the first time, has expanded its UK workforce and agreed to establish local production of its Barracuda-500M cruise missile in Poland.

"Each government has a different localisation need," said Anduril UK General Manager Richard Drake.

EUROPE STRIVES FOR INDEPENDENCE

But some Europeans worry that the U.S. could be less willing or able to provide weapons, parts or other ​support ​in the future, including if American defence companies need to prioritise U.S. military needs in ​other regions.

Europeans no longer want finished products, they want access to ‌enough of the underlying technology to build, modify and maintain equipment themselves, industry insiders and specialists say. They want "a significant IP transfer," said Fabio Dal Pan, a Milan-based senior partner at Boston Consulting Group, a management consulting firm.

title: The Hundred: New era, familiar result for London Spirit as Liam Livingstone heroics fall short
description: Liam Livingstone produced a superb all-round display with 69 off 40 balls and 2 for 14, but it wasn't enough as London Spirit slipped to a seven-run defeat against Manchester Super Giants in their Hundred opener. Spirit's women also lost by seven wickets, making it a disappointing start to the new era at Lord's.
fullText:
TimesofIndia.com in London: New owners, new coaches, new players and a new captain. London Spirit arrived at Lord's on Thursday promising a fresh start, but their opening day of The Hundred 2026 produced a painfully familiar result.

For the fifth time in six seasons, Spirit's men began their campaign with defeat as Manchester Super Giants edged a thriller by seven runs in front of 23,847 spectators. Earlier, Spirit's women had been comprehensively beaten by seven wickets, completing a double defeat for the hosts.

In between came a distinctly Hundred-style interlude, with rapper Tinie Tempah performing amid jets of fire and even venturing into the Lord's crowd. But once attention returned to the cricket, it was Liam Livingstone who provided the evening's real entertainment.

Spirit's new captain almost single-handedly dragged his side towards victory with an extraordinary all-round performance.

Having put Manchester in, Spirit were initially made to toil by Tim Seifert, who marked his first Hundred appearance with 67 from 45 balls. The New Zealander added 49 with Jos Buttler (16) and 40 with Heinrich Klaasen (17) as the visitors reached 103 for two.

That was when Livingstone took matters into his own hands.

The captain bowled 20 of the final 25 deliveries, conceding only 14 runs and taking two wickets as Manchester spectacularly lost seven wickets for 35 runs. Six of those fell for just 22 runs in the final 26 balls, leaving the visitors on 138 for nine.

On a Lord's surface where batters struggled for timing, only four days after England and India had combined for 747 runs in an ODI, Manchester's total appeared around par.

Spirit's chase quickly ran into trouble when James Rew departed for a two-ball duck. Livingstone rebuilt alongside Kiran Carlson (19) before adding 68 with Dewald Brevis, although the South African's 22 came from 23 balls as the required rate climbed.

With 56 needed from 30 balls, Livingstone shifted gears.

He took 12 from Noor Ahmad's final five deliveries and brought up his half-century from 32 balls with a trademark slog sweep. Manchester also gave him a helping hand, most notably when Seifert spilled a chance at deep midwicket and watched the ball bounce over the boundary for six.

Suddenly, Spirit were back in it.

They required 21 from the final 10 deliveries, but Manchester's England pace duo held their nerve. Gus Atkinson removed Brevis with a caught-and-bowled dismissal and finished with figures of two for 15, leaving Sonny Baker to defend 12 from the final five balls.

Baker had conceded 25 runs from his first 15 deliveries, while Livingstone had already struck five sixes.

This time, however, the 23-year-old seamer won the battle. After conceding three runs from his first two deliveries, Baker went full and fast and crashed into Livingstone's stumps. James Coles was caught off the final ball as Spirit finished on 131 for six.

Livingstone's 69 from 40 balls, coupled with figures of two for 14, earned him the Match Hero award but not the result.

"We bowled some really good stuff through the middle, dragged it back towards the end, and we nearly chased it down," Livingstone said. "We just got a bit too far behind the rate to catch up in the end."

There was considerably less drama in the women's game.

Grace Harris struck the opening delivery for four, but Spirit promptly collapsed to 23 for four in the powerplay and were eventually bowled out for 80 in 91 balls.

Manchester needed only 59 deliveries to complete a seven-wicket win, with Paige Scholfield finishing the chase with successive four and six.

For London Spirit, it was a sobering beginning to what was supposed to be a fresh chapter. Livingstone believes there is something to build on, and his own performance certainly provided encouragement.

But for all the changes around Lord's, opening night brought the same old outcome: two games, two defeats.

The Hundred men's competition, Lord's

London Spirit 131-6 (100 balls): Livingstone 69 (40); Atkinson 2-15

Manchester Super Giants won by seven runs

Manchester Super Giants beat London Spirit by seven runs in The Hundred at Lord's as Liam Livingstone's big-hitting innings came in vain.

The home captain's 40-ball knock of 69 from number four, preceded by bowling figures of 2-14 in Super Giants' innings, kept his side in contention as they chased 139.

Coming in after James Rew was dismissed for a two-ball duck, Livingstone put on 37 with Kiran Carlson (19) and 68 with Dewald Brevis.

South Africa international Brevis played junior partner, scoring 22 off 23 balls, before being caught and bowled by Gus Atkinson, who took 2-15, in the penultimate set.

Needing 12 off the final five balls, Livingstone faced England seamer Sonny Baker, who had conceded 25 runs from his first 15 deliveries.

Livingstone had already struck five sixes in his innings and was looking to go big again.

It was 23-year-old Baker who came out on top, though, conceding just four more runs, bowling Livingstone and then having James Coles caught from the final delivery of the match as Spirit finished on 131-6.

Having been put in to bat earlier, Super Giants captain Aiden Markram made a slow start, scoring one off 10 by the time he was trapped lbw by Adam Milne, but opening partner Tim Seifert fared rather better.

The New Zealander struck 67 from 45 deliveries, sharing partnerships of 49 and 40 with Jos Buttler (16) and Heinrich Klaasen (17).

However, no further batters made it to double figures, with Spirit losing seven wickets for 35 runs as they tallied 138-9.

Seifert's wicket was the seventh to fall when he was caught at mid-wicket by David Willey off Coles, but he had ultimately helped set a winning total for the visitors.

Olympic medallists Alex Yee and Beth Potter will be competing at the World Triathlon Championship Series in London this weekend, and you can follow the action live on the BBC.

Paris 2024 gold medallist Yee returns after competing in marathons and more recently, the 5,000m in the Monaco Diamond League.

Fellow Briton Potter tops the women's standings and world rankings after three podium places in the opening rounds of the series.

The WTCS represents the flagship elite series of World Triathlon, with the world's best triathletes competing at iconic venues including the ExCeL London.

A further three races are planned for the season, which culminates with the finals in Pontevedra, Spain, in September.

Potter will be among the favourites to win on British soil, despite missing June's Quiberon race in France because of altitude training and finishing sixth in the previous meeting in Hamburg.

The Glaswegian, who claimed bronze in the Paris 2024 Olympics, won the season opener in Uzbekistan and came second in both the Japan and Sardinia races.

Since delivering one of the standout moments of the Paris Games, Yee has experimented with marathon running – making his debut in the London 2025 race and then achieving the second-fastest time by a Briton in Valencia 2025, running 2:06:38.

The 28-year-old began his transition back to triathlon in Yokohama where he finished fifth. But the Olympic champion failed to finish the men's race in Sardinia.

title: The borough where families are slowly disappearing
description: Islington is a snapshot of a trend playing out across inner London, Britain and much of the world.
fullText:
Islington seems, on the surface, a family-friendly area. Parents push buggies through quiet leafy side streets of this popular neighbourhood that is also within easy reach of central London.

But this north London borough has one of the lowest fertility rates in the country and mothers are older on average here than in most other parts of the capital.

Islington is a snapshot of a trend also playing out not only in inner London but also other parts of the world.

The situation has been described by the London Assembly as an "existential challenge" for the city as a whole, so what are the reasons behind this and what can be done about it?

Keen to find out more about family life in Islington, I joined a Zip-Zap baby music class to speak to parents.

Tiphanie Frutuoso and her husband had their first baby this year.

"My husband and I have a one-bedroom flat – a two-bedroom is super expensive.

"Childcare is £2,000-£3,000 a month."

They are moving back to Luxembourg, partly because childcare is free.

"It's really sad because we love London. We have better job opportunities here," Frutuoso added.

Tina Meschino had her first child at 41.

"I've always been career-driven. I moved to London from Australia for career opportunities.

"It's taken a while to get to where I want to be – an executive position – which felt like the right time to start a family."

But she added that it was very difficult to find a suitable home with enough space, within budget.

Samantha Nagaratnam had her daughter at 35.

"I was moving forward in my career and was really, really focused on that. But nobody tells you how hard it is [to fall pregnant]. It took about three years when we started trying."

Originally from Toronto, she said it was much harder to find a family home in Islington with enough space.

Zip-Zap co-founder Laura Edwards says families are moving out of Islington to other boroughs for better schools, more affordable homes and more space.

"It's going to have huge implications in 40-50 years when there's nobody to do the jobs and support the economy."

Some families have told me they have decided to stay in the borough but it is proving to be really difficult.

Father-of-two Patrick Penny-Annang has lived in Islington all his life and now shares a one-bedroom flat with his family.

"Our living room becomes our bedroom... our one bed becomes the kids' room," he said.

"Islington is a lovely area to live in but because of that it's really expensive.

"Schools have been closing, schools that I used to go to."

Between 2013 and 2023, London's population of 0–9-year-olds fell by 99,100, despite the capital's overall population growing by 506,000. The decline has been steeper in inner than outer London.

"It's an existential challenge for London," says Bassam Mahfouz, chairman of the London Assembly's Economy, Culture and Skills Committee.

His committee's recent report recommends pursuing UNICEF Child Friendly City status, introducing child-friendly housing standards, and mapping play and recreation spaces across boroughs.

"We need to tackle this as an absolute emergency.

"What's happening in Islington is happening right across London," he said, warning the trend threatens the city's workforce.

He is urging the government and the mayor to "redouble their efforts" to ensure "children are growing up in every postcode".

The fertility rate measures the number of children born per woman of childbearing age.

At 0.99, Islington has the second-lowest total fertility rate in the capital after the City of London, and one of the lowest in England.

To put it in perspective, the estimated number of children born per woman fell to just under 1.4 for England and Wales in 2025, down from 1.9 in 2010.

BBC England's data unit analysed some of the factors that may be contributing to Islington's low rate:

Young women leaving: In 2025, Islington recorded a net loss of 1,062 women aged 30-34, one of the biggest declines for that age group in the country

High rents: In 2023-24, renters spent 46% of the median local income on rent, giving Islington the ninth-highest rent-to-income ratio among 316 councils in England and Wales and only eight boroughs – all in London – ranked higher

Unaffordable housing: In 2025, the median house price was almost 12 times the median annual income, placing Islington among the 40 least affordable local authorities in England

Social housing demand: As of 31 March 2025, 16,794 households were on Islington's social housing waiting list – the 17th highest in England and sixth highest in London

Expensive childcare: Parents paid an average £9.39 an hour for two-year-olds - the 12th highest in England.

Francesca Baker-Brooker, 39, who works in PR, and her husband Andy, 41, an accountant, have decided not to have children.

The couple live in a two-bedroom flat in Islington. They both say they shared a "gut instinct" early in their relationship that parenthood was not for them.

"We like our lifestyle - we like running, going to festivals and gigs," Francesca said.

Soon after that conversation, they moved from a three-bedroom house in Kent to a two-bedroom flat in Islington and Andy had a vasectomy.

"I don't know how feasible it would have been to move to London if we'd wanted to start a family," Andy said.

When people ask if he has a family, Andy says his answer is: "I have a family – my wife."

They say about half of their friends in London do not have children, although they believe that is far less common outside the capital.

"I think it definitely is easier to be child-free in London," he added.

Katie Beck, a policy fellow at the London School of Economics' LSE Cities, said: "People want to have children in London, but there are barriers – namely the cost of living and childcare.

"People are not able to stay in London to have children, or once they do they're moving to outer boroughs or leaving London altogether."

Beck says London's falling rates of children reflects a wider global trend, driven by housing and childcare costs, more women entering higher education and the workforce, changing parenting expectations, fewer teenage pregnancies, and growing concerns about the future.

She points to boroughs such as Islington, where high poverty, limited green space, expensive housing and dense populations contribute to particularly low child populations.

I was keen to find out what the younger generation think, so spoke to a group of students.

Jess Rolf, 23, says having children was "never something she worried about", and trying to build a settled life was "very stressful with the cost of living and the job market".

"I'm from Lincolnshire and people my age back home are buying houses with their partners and talking about starting families.

"I don't think that's on the cards for me."

Charlotte Ward, 26, has said planning ahead is difficult.

"A lot of people our age are quite disenfranchised.

"You put all your energy into school, university and work, then wonder, 'do I want to bring somebody else into that if I can't even support myself right now?'

"When parents or grandparents ask 'what happens when you have children?', I can say, 'I might not'.

"There's a small element of emancipation from the expectation that you definitely will have children but if I'm progressing in my career and my male counterparts don't have to take time out to have a child, that could put me at a disadvantage."

Millicent Angel, 24, says it is hard to envisage a future when the world feels "so unstable" but she still definitely wants children.

She adds there's "a million and one things" she would like to do first, including developing her career.

Beck argues that "children are an indicator species".

"They are a sign of a healthy city. If you see a dearth of children, that rings alarm bells that a city is not functioning as it should," she added.

She describes a child-friendly city as one that is accessible, with active transport and safe affordable housing.

As the independent think tank Centre for London points out: "London is not becoming a city without families with children, but it is becoming a place where the realities that families with children face are increasingly unequal."

A spokesperson for the Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan said: "The mayor wants London to remain a city for everyone – where people can afford to put down roots, raise a family and build a future.

"That is why tackling London's housing crisis and increasing the supply of genuinely affordable homes is one of his top priorities, alongside measures to support families with the cost of living, including funding free school meals for every child in a state primary school."

They added that he would "continue working with the government to build more affordable homes, support public services and ensure London remains a great place for families and children".

A government spokesperson said: "We've made paternity and unpaid parental leave day one rights through our Employment Rights Act, and have rolled out 30 hours of funded childcare a week to working families."

The government added that it was also building more council homes to back "families at every stage".

title: UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital
description: The health worker was evacuated to the UK from the DR Congo after being potentially exposed to the virus.
fullText:
A humanitarian worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been medically evacuated to the UK after a potential healthcare‑related exposure to Ebola.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the individual, who is a UK resident and has not been named, has no symptoms, and the move is purely precautionary.

The individual remains well but is being assessed and monitored at a London hospital, the statement from UKHSA said.

The hospital has not been named but the Royal Free in north London has a high level isolation unit and is the primary national centre for high consequence infectious diseases.

The incubation period of Ebola ranges from two to 21 days and the humanitarian worker will be required to isolate throughout.

The individual had been working with a humanitarian organisation supporting the Ebola outbreak response.

Ebola is a highly dangerous pathogen. Unlike flu or Covid, it is not airborne and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids.

Symptoms come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

Richard Pebody, director of epidemic and emerging infections at UKHSA, said: "The risk to the general public remains low.

"This individual has been transferred out of an abundance of caution, and we're pleased they remain well."

There are currently no confirmed cases of Ebola in the UK, the agency said.

There were three confirmed Ebola cases in the UK between 2014 and 2015 - all involving healthcare workers returning from west Africa. All recovered and there was no onward transmission.

According to the World Health Organization, as of 19 July the DR Congo government has recorded 2,423 confirmed cases of Ebola, including 967 deaths, since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. The WHO said 469 had recovered.

Uganda has recorded another 20 confirmed cases and two deaths.

The latest outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which there is no vaccine, although several are in development.

It has been described as the third-worst outbreak on record by WHO head Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.

title: Murdered ex-UK minister Widdecombe was struck on head with hammer 21 times, court told
description: LONDON, July 21 (Reuters) - Former British government minister Ann Widdecombe was killed by a man who struck her on the head 21 times with a hammer while ‌she was eating lunch at home earlier this mon...
fullText:
LONDON, July 21 (Reuters) - Former British government minister Ann Widdecombe was killed by a man who struck her on the head 21 times with a hammer while ‌she was eating lunch at home earlier this month, prosecutors told a London court on Tuesday.

Widdecombe, ‌78, a prominent figure in Nigel Farage's populist Reform UK party, was found dead at her home in rural southwest ​England on July 9 after being attacked the day before.

The killing shocked British politics, raising further concerns about politicians' security, with two serving British members of parliament having been killed since 2016.

Joshua Kerry, a white British national from Rotherham in northern England, more than 250 miles (402 km) from Widdecombe's home, appeared in ‌court on Tuesday charged with her ⁠murder.

The bearded 28-year-old, who appeared in the dock at London's Westminster Magistrates' Court wearing a grey tracksuit, was not asked to enter a plea.

At a later ⁠hearing at the Old Bailey court, Kerry was remanded in custody until his next appearance in October.

Police have said they believe Widdecombe was targeted, although the motive remains under investigation. Prosecutors said an investigation into possible ​terrorism ​offences was ongoing.

CAMERA IN HOME CAPTURED INCIDENT

Prosecutor Kashif Malik ​earlier said a camera inside Widdecombe's home ‌had captured the attack.

Widdecombe had been due to be interviewed live on television on July 8 from her home but did not appear, Malik explained. The following day, her personal assistant asked her gardener to check on Widdecombe, and he found her on the kitchen floor.

Malik told the court that the recovered footage showed Kerry entering Widdecombe's home while she was eating lunch and asking: "Don't suppose you ‌have bank cards and ID?"

Kerry, who was wearing black ​gloves and holding a hammer to his side so it ​was hidden from Widdecombe's view, then struck ​her 21 times, Malik said.

He added that Kerry had tipped Widdecombe out of ‌her chair onto the floor before taking ​her wallet and leaving, having ​been in the property for approximately two minutes.

Widdecombe was known for her socially conservative views, first as a junior minister in Conservative Prime Minister John Major's 1992-1997 government and later ​as an immigration and justice ‌spokesperson for Reform UK.

After stepping down from parliament in 2010, she appeared in a number ​of reality TV shows, including "Strictly Come Dancing".

The Blues completed the signing of England midfielder Rogers from Aston Villa for a British record transfer fee of £117m on Monday.

It had been widely expected that Rogers, who was Villa's most prized asset, would be available only for an English transfer record fee, but many expected Arsenal to be the frontrunners.

However, Chelsea had been tracking Rogers for more than two years and had quietly made him their top attacking target with a combined effort involving the club's sporting directors, Alonso and co-owner Behdad Eghbali helping to secure a deal.

"I'm so excited," Rogers said on the move.

"For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started.

"I'm a free spirit, free-flowing footballer. I like to take risks, make things happen, change games. Whatever that may take. Just can't wait to get started."

title: UK politician Ann Widdecombe was struck 21 times with a hammer, court hears
description: Ann Widdecombe, the former British lawmaker found dead at her home in southwest England in early July, was hit 21 times with a hammer, a London court heard
fullText:
Ann Widdecombe, the former British lawmaker found dead at her home in southwest England in early July, was hit 21 times with a hammer, a London court heard on Tuesday.

Joshua Kerry, 28, allegedly entered Widdecombe's house in the village of Haytor Vale on July 8, Prosecutor Kashif Malik told Westminster Magistrates' Court, according to UK news agency PA Media.

He then allegedly walked into the 78-year-old politician's kitchen wielding a hammer and repeatedly struck her head while she was eating lunch, the court heard.

He was only in her home for two minutes, the court heard.

Widdecombe's provisional cause of death was described in court as a "blunt force injury to the head."

Kerry then appeared at London's Old Bailey criminal court, where he was denied bail and remanded in custody. A case management hearing is scheduled for October 9, and a provisional trial date is set for 8 June 2027.

British counterterrorism police took over the investigation into Widdecombe's killing on July 13, after officers initially stated there was no information to suggest her death was an act of terrorism.

Her death came against a backdrop of increased violence and heightened threat against lawmakers in Britain. She is the third Member of Parliament to have been killed in recent years, following Sir David Amess and Jo Cox.

Sam Curran's all-round brilliance led MI London to a convincing seven-wicket win over Sunrisers Leeds in the opening match of the men's Hundred.

Chasing 144, Curran finished unbeaten on 60 as MI London eased to their target with 16 balls remaining.

After Brydon Carse's fine spell of 2-18 had given Sunrisers hope, Curran added 93 from just 40 balls for the fourth wicket with Nicholas Pooran.

The destructive Pooran struck a magnificent 19-ball fifty which took the game from Sunrisers, as he clubbed five fours and five sixes in his 58 not out.

Curran had earlier taken 2-27 and seamer Richard Gleeson also impressed with 4-25 as Sunrisers were bowled out for 143.

Mitchell Marsh top-scored with 41 at the top of the order but Sunrisers struggled for momentum after his departure, though Tom Alsop's cameo of 31 from 18 balls gave them a late boost.

England white-ball captain Harry Brook fell for eight and Sunrisers skipper Zak Crawley only managed 13.

MI London, who were previously known as Oval Invincibles prior to the private investment in the Hundred, have won the past three men's tournaments.

title: New UK leader Burnham says he will never take risks with economy
description: LONDON, July 20 () - Britain's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, said on Monday he would never take risks with the economy, re-committing to ‌a pledge to stick to the previous government's fiscal rule...
fullText:
LONDON, July 20 (Reuters) - Britain's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, said on Monday he would never take risks with the economy, re-committing to ‌a pledge to stick to the previous government's fiscal rules.

Burnham has promised ‌measures to help with the cost of living while sticking to the fiscal rules, chief among them ​a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with revenue by the end of the decade, and to election pledges not to raise taxes on working people.

Asked how he might do more while still meeting those fiscal rules and whether that meant more borrowing in ‌order to invest, Burnham told ⁠reporters: "I think you've jumped ahead a bit there because I've said we'll stick to ... the existing fiscal rules and use obviously ⁠any flexibility within them.

"So none of this is about taking risks with the economy. I've never done that in any role that I've had. I've always taken a very ​prudent approach."

Earlier, ​in his first speech outside his new ​Downing Street office, Burnham indicated he ‌would aim to reduce welfare spending to stay within the fiscal rules and meet Britain's commitments on defence.

He offered little detail on his future policy plans but said he would try to offer people in Britain some "breathing space" from a cost-of-living crisis with immediate measures to be announced from Tuesday.

Burnham told reporters he was "finalising" the details ‌of those measures, declining to detail what they ​might be.

"But we just want to do some ​things that people will feel ​and feel quite quickly," he said.

"It won't solve everything, it won't ‌take all of the pressure off, ​but it just shows ​the direction of travel and ... about helping them out."

Burnham was looking at the "personal allowance" threshold at which people start paying income tax which successive governments ​have frozen, dragging more people ‌into paying tax as their incomes go up.

"It's difficult because changing ​the threshold is not without significant consequences," he said. "But I'm looking at ​it."
